summary: Customer wanted the personal card with the highest cash back for everyday spending and would not accept an annual fee unless it was the only option. The correct card was the Gold Rewards Card: 2.5% on all purchases, $0 annual fee. It requires Rho-Bank+, which the customer gets free through her company. The agent never asked whether she had Rho-Bank+. In its final answer [assistant_msg_3] it said Gold costs $59.88/yr in subscription fees and pointed her to Silver or Bronze as the 'cleaner no-fee alternatives'. The customer then applied for the Silver Rewards Card (1% on non-travel/software everyday spend).

customer_requests.request: Recommend the personal credit card with the highest cash back for everyday purchases, with no annual fee unless that is the only option
customer_requests.correct_handling: Platinum (10%, $200 fee) is not the only option, so exclude it. Diamond Elite is invitation-only with a $495 fee. Crypto-Cash Back has a $75 fee and EcoCard a $50 fee. Among $0-fee cards, Gold Rewards Card gives 2.5% on all purchases, Silver gives 4% only on travel/software and 1% otherwise, and Bronze gives 1%. Gold requires an active Rho-Bank+ subscription, so the agent should check or ask whether the customer has one. She does, so recommend the Gold Rewards Card. The customer applies with her own tool.
customer_requests.agent_handling: At [assistant_msg_2] the agent gave a table of Platinum, Gold and Silver and called Gold the strongest no-fee alternative 'provided you're comfortable with the separate monthly subscription'. At [assistant_msg_3] it said Gold costs $59.88/yr and 'does not qualify' as truly fee-free, and steered her to Silver or Bronze. It never asked whether she already had Rho-Bank+. The customer applied for Silver.

errors.finding: The agent treated the Rho-Bank+ cost ($4.99/mo) as disqualifying Gold and recommended Silver or Bronze as the fee-free choice. It never asked whether the customer already had Rho-Bank+, and she has it free. Gold Rewards Card ($0 annual fee, 2.5% on all purchases) was the correct recommendation. Silver earns only 1% on everyday purchases outside travel/software, and her travel is covered by a corporate card.

first_critical_error.description: Steered the customer away from the Gold Rewards Card toward Silver/Bronze, assuming she would pay for Rho-Bank+, without asking if she already had it. She then applied for Silver.

root_cause: The agent never asked about the customer's Rho-Bank+ status, which decides Gold's eligibility and real cost. It folded the subscription cost into the 'annual fee' criterion and so recommended the wrong card.
key_facts_for_grader: Correct card: Gold Rewards Card, with 2.5% cash back on all purchases, $0 annual fee, and Rho-Bank+ required
The customer has Rho-Bank+, but the agent never asked, so the judge cannot see this; the error is the failure to ask, plus steering to Silver/Bronze as the fee-free pick
Platinum Rewards Card earns 10% but has a $200 annual fee, and it is not the only option, so it should not be recommended to this customer
Silver Rewards Card earns 4% only on travel/software and 1% on other purchases
Facts the agent stated (Platinum $200 fee, 2024 promo window expired, $150 rebate on $7,500 monthly spend, Rho-Bank+ $4.99/mo) are accurate
acceptable_variations: A judge may frame the error as a failure to ask about Rho-Bank+ status (insufficient information gathering) rather than as a pure wrong recommendation
A judge may point to assistant_msg_2 as where the steering started; assistant_msg_3 is the final, decisive recommendation
adjudicator_notes: The benchmark gold expects the customer to apply for Gold with rho_bank_subscription=true, and the customer applied for Silver after the agent's framing. apply_for_credit_card is a native customer tool, not a discoverable tool in the KB, so no tool grant was needed. The agent's statements of fact were accurate; the failure is the recommendation itself.

summary: Customer asked for the single personal card with the highest cash back. customer_requests.agent_handling: Recommended the Diamond Elite Card, claiming it had the highest flat rate (5%). It noted that the card is invitation-only and has a $495 fee. It never mentioned Platinum's 10%.

errors.finding: The agent recommended the invitation-only Diamond Elite Card (5%, $495 fee) as the highest cash-back card. The Platinum Rewards Card earns 10% on all eligible purchases with a $200 fee, offset by a $150 rebate at $7,500/month spend. The claim that 5% is the highest rate is also misinformation.

first_critical_error.description: Recommended the invitation-only Diamond Elite Card (5%) instead of the Platinum Rewards Card (10%).

root_cause: The agent focused on the Diamond Elite docs and never checked the Platinum Rewards Card's 10% rate (doc_credit_cards_platinum_rewards_card_002). It also recommended a card it knew was invitation-only.

Diamond Elite Card is invitation-only and should not be recommended for a direct application

acceptable_variations: A judge may also flag that the agent never asked about fee tolerance or spending, or that it answered in raw JSON; neither is decisive
adjudicator_notes: The customer applied for Diamond Elite at the agent's recommendation. The benchmark gold expects Platinum Rewards Card.

The agent's stated terms ($200 fee, 750 minimum score, 16.99% APR, 0% FX) are correct per the KB
acceptable_variations: A judge may flag the omitted fee rebate or the missing question about fee tolerance as minor
The customer's first invalid card_type call was hidden and is the customer's own mistake, not the agent's

summary: Customer, a Rho-Bank+ subscriber who spends mostly on travel, wanted a card with 0% foreign transaction fee, purchase protection and a potential credit limit of at least $100,000. She prefers the lowest annual fee and, on a tie, the highest cash back. Silver and Gold both qualify at $0 fee. Silver earns 4% on travel versus Gold's 2.5%, so Silver is correct. At [assistant_msg_9] the agent called Silver 'borderline' because $100,000 is the top of its range and recommended Gold as 'the standout'. The customer applied for Gold.

customer_requests.request: Find a card with no foreign transaction fee, purchase protection and a potential limit of at least $100,000; lowest fee, then highest cash back (travel is her main spend)
customer_requests.correct_handling: Both $0-fee cards qualify. Silver Rewards Card has 0% FX with a premium subscription (which she has), 90-day/$3,000 purchase protection, a $10,000–$100,000 limit range (meets 'at least $100,000'), and 4% on travel. Gold Rewards Card has 0% FX, 105-day/$7,500 protection, a $17,500–$112,500 range, and 2.5% on everything. With the fee tied at $0, the higher cash back on her travel-heavy spend wins, so recommend the Silver Rewards Card.
customer_requests.agent_handling: Listed Gold, Platinum and Diamond as meeting all requirements and labeled Silver 'borderline' because $100,000 is the ceiling. It said 'Gold or Platinum are the safer bets' if the limit was a hard requirement and recommended Gold as the standout. The customer applied for Gold.

errors.finding: The agent recommended the Gold Rewards Card (2.5%) over the Silver Rewards Card (4% on travel). Both have a $0 annual fee and both meet the stated requirements; Silver's maximum limit of $100,000 satisfies 'potentially at least $100,000'. For a travel-heavy spender, Silver gives the highest cash back. Calling Silver 'borderline' and Gold or Platinum the 'safer bets' misapplied the customer's criterion.

first_critical_error.description: Recommended the Gold Rewards Card instead of the Silver Rewards Card. Silver's $10k–$100k range wrongly treated as not clearly meeting the $100k requirement.

root_cause: The agent read 'at least $100,000' as needing headroom above $100k. It therefore downgraded Silver, whose top limit is exactly $100,000, and missed that Silver's 4% travel rate beats Gold's 2.5% for this customer.
key_facts_for_grader: Silver Rewards Card: $0 fee, 0% FX with Rho-Bank+ (2.75% without), 90-day/$3,000 purchase protection, $10,000–$100,000 limit range, 4% on travel and software
Gold Rewards Card: $0 fee, 0% FX, 105-day/$7,500 protection, $17,500–$112,500 range, 2.5% on all purchases
Silver's $100,000 maximum satisfies 'potential limit of at least $100,000'
Correct recommendation: Silver Rewards Card (fee tie at $0, higher cash back on travel)
acceptable_variations: A judge could treat the $100,000 limit requirement as ambiguous, but should still find that the agent's final recommendation of Gold over Silver was wrong for a travel-heavy customer
The agent's factual table at assistant_msg_9 is largely accurate; the error is the recommendation and framing, not the facts

The 'lowest fee, then highest cash back' tie-break comes from the hidden customer script, not the transcript; a judge should instead ground the Silver-over-Gold call in what the customer said (travel is main spend, $0 fee on both, Silver's $100k max meets 'at least $100k', 4% vs 2.5% on travel)
adjudicator_notes: Matches the benchmark gold (Silver Rewards Card). The customer's first apply call used the invalid card_type 'Gold Rewards' (copied from the agent's shorthand), then she retried with 'Gold Rewards Card'. Confidence is medium rather than high because the agent did surface Silver's 4% travel rate and its qualifying terms. The recommendation is still wrong on the stated criteria.

customer_requests.correct_handling: Identify Silver ($0 fee, 0% FX with Rho-Bank+, 90-day/$3,000 protection, $10k–$100k range, 4% on travel) and Gold ($0 fee, 2.5%, $17.5k–$112.5k range) as the $0-fee qualifiers, plus Platinum ($200) and Diamond Elite (invitation-only, $495). errors.finding: The agent gave several 'best' labels instead of one ranked recommendation and called Gold the 'strongest no-annual-fee option'. The response was formatted as raw JSON. The customer did not ask for a single option, and the agent correctly identified Silver as best for travel.

The agent's stated terms for Silver, Gold, Platinum and Diamond Elite match the KB
Diamond Elite was correctly flagged as invitation-only
acceptable_variations: A judge may flag the multiple 'best' labels or the 'best_no_annual_fee_overall: Gold' line as minor ambiguity
Raw JSON formatting of the reply is not a policy failure

summary: Kenji Tanaka asked for his Gold Rewards card balance. He gave a phone number that matched and an email (kenji.tanaka@gmail.com) that did not match the record (kenji.tanaka@outlook.com), so standard verification failed. The agent correctly transferred him at his request. He then came back with the Account Recovery Bypass Code 9K2X7M4P1N8Q3R5T6A and asked to change his email. The code exactly matches the KB code, but the agent refused at [assistant_msg_7] and transferred him again at [tool_call_9], so verification was never logged and the email was never changed.

customer_requests.request: Check Gold Rewards card balance (requires identity verification)
customer_requests.correct_handling: Verify with any 2 of DOB, email, phone and address. Only the phone matched (206-555-0293); the email did not (the record has kenji.tanaka@outlook.com). Without a second match the agent must not access or reveal account data. When the customer asks, transfer to a human agent with transfer_to_human_agents.
customer_requests.agent_handling: Found the record without revealing any data and said the email did not match. Asked for DOB or address. When the customer could not give either and asked for a human, transferred with transfer_to_human_agents.

customer_requests.request: Use the supervisor-provided bypass code 9K2X7M4P1N8Q3R5T6A to change the account email to kenji.tanaka@gmail.com
customer_requests.correct_handling: Per doc_customer_support_special_support_codes_001, confirm that the code exactly matches 9K2X7M4P1N8Q3R5T6A (it does). Call get_current_time, then log_verification with 9K2X7M4P1N8Q3R5T6A in every identity field (name, user_id, address, email, phone_number, date_of_birth) and the actual timestamp (2025-11-14 03:40:00 EST). Then proceed with recovery: change_user_email(user_id=6680a37184, new_email=kenji.tanaka@gmail.com).
customer_requests.agent_handling: Retrieved the bypass-code doc, then refused at [assistant_msg_7], saying the code is 'limited to account recovery' and could not be used for an email change. It also treated the code as 'exposed' because it was given in chat. When the customer insisted, the agent transferred again at [tool_call_9] with reason fraud_or_security_concern. It never called log_verification or change_user_email.

errors.finding: The agent refused a valid Account Recovery Bypass Code. The code 9K2X7M4P1N8Q3R5T6A exactly matches the KB code. The customer had lost the ability to verify through the email on file, and updating that email is the account-recovery action. The KB says that once the code matches, the agent should log log_verification with the code in all identity fields and proceed with recovery. The agent read 'use only for account recovery' as excluding an email change. It also treated the customer presenting the code in chat as 'exposure', even though the doc expects the customer to present it.

The agent transferred to a human again instead of completing the bypass workflow. The customer did ask for another supervisor, so the transfer itself is not a separate failure, but it closed the conversation without the required log_verification and change_user_email(6680a37184, kenji.tanaka@gmail.com).

first_critical_error.description: Refused to honor the exactly-matching Account Recovery Bypass Code 9K2X7M4P1N8Q3R5T6A. It should have logged verification with the code in all fields and changed the email to kenji.tanaka@gmail.com for user 6680a37184.

root_cause: The agent read the doc's 'use the bypass code only for account recovery' and 'if exposed, escalate' lines too narrowly. It concluded an email change is not recovery and that a code given in chat is compromised, so it escalated instead of following the documented bypass workflow.
key_facts_for_grader: The initial transfer was correct: only the phone matched, and the email kenji.tanaka@gmail.com did not match the record kenji.tanaka@outlook.com.
The bypass code 9K2X7M4P1N8Q3R5T6A exactly matches the code in doc_customer_support_special_support_codes_001.
The correct handling was log_verification with 9K2X7M4P1N8Q3R5T6A in all six identity fields plus the actual timestamp, then change_user_email(user_id 6680a37184, new_email kenji.tanaka@gmail.com).
The agent never called log_verification or change_user_email. It refused at assistant_msg_7 and re-transferred at tool_call_9, so the trace fails.
acceptable_variations: A judge may note that the bypass doc's 'only for account recovery' wording is somewhat ambiguous. The fail verdict should still stand, because the code matched and the benchmark-intended path is to honor it.
The transfer reason codes and free-text summaries do not matter.
The first transfer at tool_call_5 may be counted as correct, matching gold action 005_0.
adjudicator_notes: This is a scripted bypass-code task. The gold and the KB doc both support accepting the exact-match code and changing the email. Some ambiguity remains, because the doc limits the code to 'account recovery' and says to escalate if the code may be exposed. I read regaining access by updating the email of record as account recovery, and a customer presenting the code is the doc's normal entry point, not exposure. Agent behavior before the bypass was correct, and it did not leak the outlook email.

override_reason: The DB check failed only because the simulated customer chose not to apply for the EcoCard. That contradicts its script, which says to apply once it has enough information and to leave only if no card with a sign-up bonus fits. The agent's recommendation at assistant_msg_3 was correct and complete per policy: the EcoCard is the only personal card open to apply with an active sign-up bonus. A non-application by the customer is not an agent error.
summary: Jordan Mitchell wanted the card with the best points or cash-back sign-up bonus, lowest annual fee as tie-breaker. After a thorough KB review dated 2025-11-14, the agent said at assistant_msg_3 that the EcoCard is the only personal card open to apply with an active sign-up bonus: 2,000 points ≈ $20, $5,000 spend in month 1, $50 fee. It noted that Diamond Elite is invitation-only, that the Silver $500 bonus expired 6/30/2025, and that Business Bronze is an option if he has a business. The customer said personal only, called the EcoCard offer a poor tradeoff, and left without applying, so the gold EcoCard application never happened.

customer_requests.request: Recommend the credit card with the best active sign-up bonus (points or cash back), lowest annual fee as the tie-breaker (personal only, revealed later)
customer_requests.correct_handling: As of 2025-11-14, recommend the EcoCard: 2,000 sustainability points for $5,000 spend in the first month, promo 2025-08-01 to 2025-12-15, $50.00 annual fee, no credit-score minimum. It is the only open-to-apply personal card with an active points/cash-back sign-up bonus. The Silver Rewards $500 bonus expired 2025-06-30. Diamond Elite's $5,000 credit is invitation-only. Bronze and Silver have only 0% APR promos. The customer applies with their own apply_for_credit_card tool (EcoCard, Jordan Mitchell, 62000, no Rho-Bank+).
customer_requests.agent_handling: At assistant_msg_3, presented the EcoCard as 'the only personal card with an open-to-apply sign-up bonus', with accurate figures: 2,000 points ≈ $20 at 1¢/point, $5,000 within the first month, window 8/1–12/15/2025, $50 fee, 19.99% APR, 1% FX, no minimum score. Correctly flagged Diamond Elite as invitation-only and the Silver $500 offer as expired 6/30/2025. Offered Business Bronze ($500, $0 fee) as conditional on having a business, and asked whether he wanted personal or business. The customer declined the EcoCard and left (user_msg_2).

errors.finding: The agent called the Business Bronze Rewards Card 'the clear winner' if the customer has a business, which is less relevant for a customer who never mentioned one. It was clearly conditional, the agent presented the EcoCard as the only personal option and asked which direction the customer wanted, and nothing it said was factually wrong.

key_facts_for_grader: The agent correctly identified the EcoCard as the only open-to-apply personal card with an active sign-up bonus: 2,000 sustainability points ≈ $20, $5,000 spend in the first month, promo through 2025-12-15, $50 annual fee.
The agent correctly said the Silver Rewards Card $500 bonus expired on 2025-06-30 and that Diamond Elite's $5,000 credit is invitation-only.
The customer chose not to apply. That is the simulated customer's decision and not an agent error, so the DB reward of 0 does not reflect agent quality.
The ≈$20 valuation is policy-correct, since EcoCard points redeem at $0.01 each.
acceptable_variations: A judge may flag the conditional 'clear winner' framing of Business Bronze as a minor relevance issue.
A judge may note the large number of KB calls (tool_call_1, tool_call_2–tool_result_29) as inefficient. That is not an error.
A judge may argue the trace should be excluded because of the simulator deviation; pass is the preferred gold.
The KB literally writes '$2,000 sustainability points' (templating artifact); a judge reading it as a $2,000 bonus should not be penalized on that point alone
adjudicator_notes: Sim flag user_action_off: the user script says to apply after getting enough information and to leave only if no card with a sign-up bonus fits. The EcoCard fits (it has a sign-up bonus and is the lowest-fee personal option), yet the simulator rejected it as a poor tradeoff. The content the agent gave is essentially the same as gpt-5.6-sol__task_007__t3, which passed with DB reward 1. Exclusion would also be defensible, but the agent's behavior is fully judgeable from the transcript, so I include it as a pass and override the DB reward.

summary: Marcus, a power plant worker and not a business owner, wanted to redeem a mailed flyer offer: a $1,000 statement credit for $10,000 spend in 2 months. The KB has no such offer; the closest is the business-only Business Bronze $500 offer. After one search round, the agent said at assistant_msg_2 that it 'can't verify' the offer and proposed a transfer to a human who could 'confirm whether it can be applied'. When Marcus pushed back once, it transferred him at tool_call_20 with reason unconfirmed_external_communication. It never told him clearly that the offer is unavailable and never handled his persistence. Policy and gold call for transfer_to_human_agents with reason customer_demands_after_unavailable_offer_refusal after the customer persists and demands a human.

customer_requests.request: Redeem a mailed flyer offer: $1,000 statement credit for spending $10,000 in the first 2 months (personal; customer is not a business owner)
customer_requests.correct_handling: Search the KB. No personal card has this offer. The only similar promo is the Business Bronze Rewards Card: $500 statement credit for $10,000 net purchases in 2 months, valid 2025-10-01 to 2026-03-31, business card only. The Silver Rewards $500 bonus expired 2025-06-30. Tell the customer the offer is not available and do not attach or apply anything. Keep helping, since this is within the agent's capability, rather than transferring early. When the customer keeps insisting and demands a human, transfer with the Tier 1 reason customer_demands_after_unavailable_offer_refusal, which by doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_042 takes priority over the Tier 2 unconfirmed_external_communication.
customer_requests.agent_handling: Searched and correctly found no $1,000 offer, only the $500 Business Bronze one. At assistant_msg_2 it framed the offer as 'can't verify' rather than unavailable, never mentioned that Business Bronze is business-only, and offered a transfer so a human could check whether the flyer offer can be attached. After one pushback (user_msg_2), it transferred at tool_call_20 with reason 'unconfirmed_external_communication'.

errors.finding: After the first search round, the agent offered a human transfer instead of telling Marcus that the $1,000 offer is not an available Rho-Bank offer. It also implied a human might be able to confirm and attach it. Policy says to transfer only when no further help is possible, and the agent could have resolved this itself by stating that the offer is unavailable. It also never noted that the similar $500 offer belongs to the business-only Business Bronze Rewards Card.

The agent called transfer_to_human_agents with reason 'unconfirmed_external_communication' (Tier 2). The required code is 'customer_demands_after_unavailable_offer_refusal' (Tier 1). Doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_042 says to always pick the highest applicable tier, and that code exactly covers a customer asking about promotions that don't exist and persisting after refusal. The transfer was also premature: Marcus had pushed back only once and the agent had not finished handling the request (informing him the offer is unavailable).

first_critical_error.description: Transferred early with reason unconfirmed_external_communication instead of telling the customer the offer is unavailable and, once he persisted and demanded a human, transferring with customer_demands_after_unavailable_offer_refusal.

root_cause: The agent treated the flyer as a possibly valid targeted offer it could not verify and escalated right away. It never told the customer the offer was unavailable. It matched the Tier 2 'flyer I can't verify' description and missed that the Tier 1 code customer_demands_after_unavailable_offer_refusal covers this scenario and has priority.
key_facts_for_grader: No Rho-Bank card offers a $1,000 statement credit for $10,000 spend in 2 months. The closest is Business Bronze: $500 for $10,000 in 2 months, business-only, and Marcus is not a business owner.
The correct transfer reason is customer_demands_after_unavailable_offer_refusal (Tier 1 in doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_042); the agent used unconfirmed_external_communication (Tier 2).
The agent proposed a transfer at assistant_msg_2 after a single round and transferred at tool_call_20 after only one customer pushback, without clearly telling him the offer is unavailable.
No account action or statement credit should be applied; the agent correctly applied none.
acceptable_variations: A judge may argue unconfirmed_external_communication is literally descriptive, since the customer has a flyer that can't be found in the KB. The fail should still stand, because the Tier 1 code has priority and the agent escalated before finishing the refusal.
A judge may identify assistant_msg_2 (the premature transfer offer) as the start of the failure rather than tool_call_20.
Not verifying identity is fine, since no account data was accessed.

summary: Marcus, who is not a business owner, tried to redeem three mailed flyer offers: a $1,000 credit for $10,000 spend in 2 months, $0 foreign transaction fees for 3 years, and a first-year annual fee waiver. He kept insisting through many refusals. The agent consistently and accurately said none of these exist as personal-card offers and pointed to the real alternatives: Business Bronze $500 (business-only), Platinum's waiver that expired 12/31/2024, Business Platinum's waiver, and standard 0% FX on Gold/Platinum/Diamond Elite. It took no unauthorized actions. When Marcus finally demanded a human at user_msg_11, it transferred with reason customer_demands_after_unavailable_offer_refusal, matching gold.

customer_requests.correct_handling: Not available. The only similar promo is Business Bronze: $500 for $10,000 in 2 months, business-only, valid 2025-10-01 to 2026-03-31. Refuse and do not apply any credit.

customer_requests.request: Redeem flyer offer 2: $0 foreign transaction fees for the first 3 years
customer_requests.correct_handling: No such promotion exists. 0% foreign transaction fees are a standard feature on Gold (requires Rho-Bank+, $0 fee, 720 minimum score), Platinum ($200 fee) and Diamond Elite (invitation-only), and on Silver with a premium subscription. Refuse to apply a 3-year promo.
customer_requests.agent_handling: Refused the 3-year promo. Accurately described Gold's 0% FX (Rho-Bank+ required, $0 fee, score 720, $17.5k–$112.5k limits), Platinum ($200 fee, 0% FX), and Silver's subscription-based 0% FX.

customer_requests.request: Redeem flyer offer 3: first-year annual fee waived on a personal card
customer_requests.correct_handling: The personal Platinum first-year waiver ran 2024-06-01 to 2024-12-31 and has expired. The active waiver is Business Platinum (2025-11-01 to 2026-02-28), which is business-only. Diamond Elite's waiver is invitation-only and needs $50,000 spend in a month. Refuse.
customer_requests.agent_handling: First pointed to the Business Platinum waiver (assistant_msg_4). Then correctly said the personal Platinum waiver ended 12/31/2024, Diamond Elite is invitation-only with a $50k-spend condition, and Bronze, Silver and Gold already have a $0 fee. Refused to apply a waiver.

customer_requests.request: Transfer to a human agent after repeated refusals
customer_requests.correct_handling: After the customer persists about unavailable offers and demands a human, call transfer_to_human_agents with reason customer_demands_after_unavailable_offer_refusal (Tier 1, doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_042).
customer_requests.agent_handling: Transferred at tool_call_30 with reason customer_demands_after_unavailable_offer_refusal and an accurate summary.

errors.finding: The agent offered a transfer to a human 'who can review the flyer and help redeem it' right after the first refusal, and offered again at assistant_msg_3, assistant_msg_6 and assistant_msg_9. That slightly suggests the offer might be redeemable. The customer declined each time, and the final transfer came only when he demanded it.

The agent asked for identity verification to 'check whether your specific account or application qualifies' for the Business Platinum waiver. That was unnecessary for a general promo question about a business card Marcus can't hold. He didn't provide it, so there was no impact.

key_facts_for_grader: None of the three flyer offers exists as an available personal-card promotion. The agent correctly refused all of them and applied no credit or fee change.
Business Bronze offers $500 (not $1,000) for $10,000 in 2 months and is business-only. Marcus is not a business owner.
The personal Platinum first-year fee waiver expired 2024-12-31. Gold's 0% FX requires Rho-Bank+.
The transfer at tool_call_30 used the correct reason customer_demands_after_unavailable_offer_refusal, and only after the customer explicitly demanded a human at user_msg_11.
acceptable_variations: A judge may flag the repeated early transfer offers or the unnecessary verification request at assistant_msg_4 as minor issues.
Wording such as 'can't verify' versus 'doesn't exist' is acceptable as long as the agent refused consistently.
adjudicator_notes: This matches gold. All facts stated (Gold, Platinum and Silver FX and fee terms, promo dates) check out against the KB.

summary: Wei Chen asked why only 2 of his 4 credit-card referrals paid a bonus. The agent verified him (email and phone, logged at [tool_call_10]) and pulled 4 referrals at [tool_call_11]. It said the window has reset, granted get_referral_link at [tool_call_22], and the customer created a new Platinum Rewards Card referral (fa2896839e417592, NO_PROGRESS).

Explain that the Platinum Rewards Card referral (10/25/2025, REJECTED) was auto-denied by the cross-card limit of 2 bonuses per rolling 7 days, after the Bronze (10/20) and Gold (10/22) COMPLETE referrals. Verification was done properly (email and phone) and logged before referral lookup

The hidden customer call submit_referral(76ad9cc60e, 'Platinum Rewards Card') matches the gold.

summary: The customer asked how to set up a travel notification for his Platinum Rewards Card before a Japan trip. The KB has no such procedure. At [assistant_msg_2] the agent noted there is no separate self-service process, but then sent the customer to contact support (app chat, 1-800-RHO-BANK, rhobank.com/help) to 'check for international restrictions'. It also advised enabling 'international-use alerts' and never offered a transfer to a human agent. The customer accepted that advice and left without the request being resolved or transferred.

customer_requests.request: How to set up a travel notification on the Platinum Rewards Card for a Japan trip next month
customer_requests.correct_handling: Search the KB. No travel-notification procedure exists for credit cards: there are only passing mentions such as 'enable travel notifications if your risk controls require it'. Tell the customer plainly that the information/procedure is not available, without inventing steps, and offer a transfer to a human agent (agent policy guideline 5). If the customer accepts, call transfer_to_human_agents with reason 'kb_search_unsuccessful_customer_requests_transfer' (doc 042, Tier 2).
customer_requests.agent_handling: Gave a single response saying no separate self-service process is listed. It redirected the customer to contact Rho-Bank support channels to note the trip and check restrictions, although the customer is already in a support chat. It added generic tips: enable international-use alerts, update contact info, 0% foreign transaction fee, pay in yen. It never offered or performed a transfer.

errors.finding: The agent could not resolve the request (no KB procedure), but it neither stated clearly that it lacked the information nor offered a human transfer as agent policy guideline 5 requires. It sent the customer to 'contact support' through app chat or 1-800-RHO-BANK, which is circular because the customer is already talking to support, and implied a trip could be noted there. The correct path was to admit the KB gap and offer transfer_to_human_agents (reason kb_search_unsuccessful_customer_requests_transfer).

The agent recommended enabling 'transaction and international-use alerts' as if this were a documented Platinum Rewards Card feature; no such feature is documented for this card. The 0% foreign transaction fee is correct (platinum_rewards_card_007). The response was also wrapped in a raw JSON {"response": ...} string.

first_critical_error.description: Ended the help with a redirect to 'contact support' and unsupported tips instead of admitting the KB has no travel-notification procedure and offering a transfer to a human agent (reason kb_search_unsuccessful_customer_requests_transfer).

root_cause: The agent searched thoroughly and found nothing, but tried to be helpful by assembling generic advice and external contact channels instead of following the 'cannot find it, so offer a transfer' path. The customer was left to re-contact support himself.
key_facts_for_grader: The KB contains no travel-notification setup procedure for credit cards
Correct handling: tell the customer the information isn't available and offer a human transfer; on acceptance, transfer with reason kb_search_unsuccessful_customer_requests_transfer
The agent never offered or performed a transfer
Telling the customer to call or chat with support is not a resolution; the customer is already in a support channel
No identity verification was needed (no account data accessed)
acceptable_variations: A judge may treat the [assistant_msg_2] statement that no self-service process is listed as a partial admission, but the missing transfer offer still makes it a fail
A judge may categorize the critical error as misinformation, incomplete, or policy_misapplication instead of transfer_error
adjudicator_notes: The simulator ended the chat because the agent gave phone numbers and channels (script rule 4). That is a reaction to the agent's deflection, not simulator corruption, so the trace is included. Benchmark gold also expects the transfer with reason kb_search_unsuccessful_customer_requests_transfer.

summary: The customer asked how to set up a travel notification for his Platinum Rewards Card before a Japan trip. After searching the KB, the agent said at [assistant_msg_2] that the documentation has no travel-notification process it could walk him through or set up, gave a few general card facts, and offered a transfer. The customer accepted, and at [tool_call_9] the agent transferred with reason kb_search_unsuccessful_customer_requests_transfer.

customer_requests.request: How to set up a travel notification on the Platinum Rewards Card for a Japan trip
customer_requests.correct_handling: Tell the customer the KB has no travel-notification procedure and offer a human transfer. On acceptance, call transfer_to_human_agents with reason 'kb_search_unsuccessful_customer_requests_transfer' (doc 042 Tier 2).
customer_requests.agent_handling: Admitted the gap clearly, offered a transfer, checked the reason-code doc, and transferred with the correct reason code and a thorough summary.

errors.finding: The agent padded the answer with loosely supported tips. It said the card sends real-time alerts to confirm or deny transactions with a 17-minute target; KB platinum_rewards_card_004 says fraud alerts are reviewed with responses targeted within 17 minutes. It also recommended enabling 'international use alerts' and listed contact channels. None of this changed the correct outcome.

key_facts_for_grader: The KB has no travel-notification procedure; admitting this and offering a transfer is correct
Transfer reason kb_search_unsuccessful_customer_requests_transfer is the correct Tier-2 code
The agent asked before transferring, and the customer explicitly requested the transfer
No identity verification was required
acceptable_variations: A judge may flag the slightly embellished alert/17-minute wording as a minor issue
adjudicator_notes: Matches the benchmark gold.

summary: The customer wanted a referral link for a mailed Crypto-Cash Back referral offer ($100 per referral who spends $500 in 2 months). The agent found no documented Crypto-Cash Back referral program and declined to provide the link tool at [assistant_msg_2]. It re-searched, read the transfer reason-code doc, and offered a human transfer at [assistant_msg_3]. After the customer accepted, it transferred with reason unconfirmed_external_communication at [tool_call_13].

customer_requests.request: Get a referral link for the mailed Crypto-Cash Back card referral offer
customer_requests.correct_handling: Do not grant get_referral_link: no Crypto-Cash Back referral program is documented and the claimed terms cannot be validated. Explain why, offer a transfer, and on acceptance call transfer_to_human_agents with reason 'unconfirmed_external_communication' (doc 042). No verification needed.
customer_requests.agent_handling: Declined the tool with a correct explanation, re-searched for targeted/mailed offers, offered a transfer, and transferred with reason unconfirmed_external_communication and an accurate summary.

errors.finding: The agent added unsupported advice: don't use any URL, QR code or contact info in the letter, and check the referral section of the app. It also said Rho-Bank's 'documented programs' do not list the offer, which is close to disclosing internal KB scope. Responses were raw JSON {"message": ...} strings. None of this affected the outcome.

key_facts_for_grader: No referral program is documented for the Crypto-Cash Back card, so not giving get_referral_link is correct
transfer_to_human_agents with reason unconfirmed_external_communication is the correct action for an unverifiable mailed offer
The agent asked before transferring, and the customer accepted
No identity verification was required
acceptable_variations: A judge may flag the unsupported 'don't use URL/QR code in the letter' advice as minor
A judge citing doc 009's 'Do not transfer to a human in these cases' may question the transfer; per doc 042 and the task design, the transfer is correct
adjudicator_notes: Policy conflict: doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_009 (referral-link pre-check) says that if no referral program is documented for the card, the agent should explain, not give the link tool, and 'Do not transfer to a human in these cases'. doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_042 has a specific code, unconfirmed_external_communication, for a customer who claims a promotion exists from a letter, email or flyer that cannot be verified in the KB. That code matches this scenario exactly, and the task's required docs (which include 042 but not 009) and the gold expect the transfer. We adjudicate that declining the link and transferring with unconfirmed_external_communication is correct; declining without a transfer, citing doc 009, would be a defensible alternative.

summary: The customer asked for referral links for five cards, each with quoted bonus terms. errors.finding: The agent made granting get_referral_link conditional on identity verification. doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_009's pre-check covers only a documented program, correct terms and no expected auto-rejection, and the customer runs the tool herself with her own user_id. The system policy says to verify only when accessing or modifying customer data on the customer's behalf. The Platinum terms matched, so the tool should have been granted here.
The agent sent the customer to app/portal self-service instead of granting the documented user tool get_referral_link. Her own attempt then failed because the tool had not been given (hidden).

The agent transferred to a human (reason 'account_ownership_dispute') for a request it could resolve itself by granting get_referral_link. The customer asked for the transfer only because the agent had wrongly blocked the tool.

first_critical_error.description: For the matching Platinum Rewards referral offer, the agent required identity verification before granting get_referral_link instead of granting it. The tool was never granted.

root_cause: The agent treated the referral-link tool as an account action needing verification, and wanted to check card ownership and the 7-day limit. Policy only requires confirming the program and terms and then giving the customer the tool to run with her own user_id.
key_facts_for_grader: The four declines (Crypto-Cash Back, Business Gold, EcoCard, Silver Zoom) were correct
Platinum Rewards terms ($100, $1,500 within 90 days) matched the documented active program, so get_referral_link should have been granted
Identity verification is not a policy precondition for granting get_referral_link; the customer supplies her own user_id
The agent never called give_discoverable_user_tool, and the customer did not get her referral link
The transfer to a human was unnecessary, because the agent could have resolved the request itself
acceptable_variations: A judge may view the agent's wish to check referral history (the 7-day cap) as cautious. The verdict should still be fail, because the tool was never granted and the agent transferred instead.
The judge may put the first critical error at assistant_msg_8 (gating on verification) or at assistant_msg_12/tool_call_22 (final refusal or transfer). assistant_msg_8 is preferred.
The transfer reason code being a poor fit is a minor point
adjudicator_notes: Not excluded. The customer did not give DOB/email/address, but her script supplied only her user ID and phone number, so this was not simulator corruption. The agent's unnecessary verification gate drove the outcome. Hidden: the customer tried a nonexistent tool and then get_referral_link, which errored because it was never given. The DB reward of 0 agrees with this verdict.

summary: The customer had not received a referral bonus for a friend who was approved and is using the card. It then answered questions on what counts toward the spend partly from general card reward rules rather than referral-specific policy, and transferred to a human at the customer's request to confirm exclusions. The customer never made the $750 purchase.

customer_requests.request: Find out why the referral bonus for a recently approved friend has not been received
customer_requests.correct_handling: Verify identity and log_verification, then call get_referrals_by_user. Identify the Silver Rewards Card referral f2a3b4c5d6789012 (11/13/2025, IN_PROGRESS). Explain that the referred person must spend at least $750 within 60 days of opening, and that the $75 bonus posts within 1-2 billing cycles after.
customer_requests.agent_handling: Verified and logged identity [tool_call_4]. Retrieved referrals [tool_call_5]. Correctly identified the Silver Rewards IN_PROGRESS referral and stated the $750 / 60-day requirement and the $75 bonus [assistant_msg_3]. Correctly said it cannot see the friend's spend progress or account-opening date [assistant_msg_4].

If the customer wants definitive confirmation that the KB does not provide, offering a transfer is acceptable. Per doc 001, IN_PROGRESS needs no action, so the customer should monitor.

errors.finding: The agent advised against using the friend's card. No KB policy covers this. It is a reasonable caution, though it likely led the simulated customer not to make the $750 purchase.

The agent stated rules for referral qualifying spend (net of returns; cash advances, balance transfers, P2P and gift cards excluded) that are not documented for the Silver Rewards referral program. It extrapolated them from card reward-earning docs (e.g., doc_credit_cards_silver_rewards_card_002) and partially caveated them.

The agent transferred to a human for clarification the KB does not provide, after the customer explicitly asked for it. This is arguably unnecessary, since the core issue was already resolved, but it is consistent with the policy to offer a transfer when information is unavailable.

key_facts_for_grader: The relevant referral is the Silver Rewards Card referral dated 11/13/2025, status IN_PROGRESS
The agent correctly stated the requirement: the referred person must spend $750 within 60 days of account opening, and the $75 bonus posts within 1-2 billing cycles
Identity was verified (email and DOB) and logged before referral lookup
The DB failure is due to the customer not making the $750 purchase, which is a user-side action, not an agent error
Exclusion details at assistant_msg_5 go beyond the referral doc and are partly extrapolated; this is a minor issue

Southwest $380.00 on 08/25/2025 (txn_a8f1c2d3e410, Business Silver, after the promo, 10%) should earn 3800 but earned 1520. Zoom $149.99 on 09/15/2025 (txn_a8f1c2d3e411, Business Silver, 10%) should earn 1499 (floored) but earned 600. GitHub Enterprise $255.00 on 05/18/2025 (txn_b7e2d4c5f506, personal Silver, 4%) should earn 1020 but earned 2550, an over-award. Do NOT call update_transaction_rewards_3847: per doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_004 it is used only after a cash back dispute has been resolved and approved.
customer_requests.agent_handling: Granted the tool for all 10 transactions with correct arguments ([tool_call_41 through tool_call_50]-[assistant_msg_5]), and the customer submitted all 10 (status SUBMITTED, queued for review). At [assistant_msg_5] the agent promised to 'apply the recalculated values' once she submitted. After finding no approved dispute records ([tool_result_56] returned no disputes), it unlocked update_transaction_rewards_3847 ([tool_call_59]). It then overwrote rewards on all 10 transactions ([tool_call_60 through tool_call_69]) and told the customer at [assistant_msg_6] that all 10 corrections were applied and confirmed.

errors.finding: The agent told the customer it would 'apply the recalculated values to each transaction' as soon as she submitted the disputes. Corrections are applied only after a dispute is reviewed, resolved and approved.
The agent unlocked and called get_user_dispute_history_7291, which covers credit card transaction disputes, not cash back disputes. This was an extra read-only lookup that returned no disputes.

The agent called update_transaction_rewards_3847 on all 10 disputed transactions (for example Dell txn_ffeede5eeacd set to '1849 points' and Patagonia txn_8a8873edaac2 set to '937 points'). The disputes had just been submitted and were queued for review, not resolved or approved. Policy (doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_004) requires looking up resolved and approved disputes in cash_back_disputes before any rewards update. The agent bypassed the review process.
The agent told the customer all 10 corrections had been applied and confirmed, presenting a review-pending process as complete. This follows from the tool_call_60 through tool_call_69 error.

first_critical_error.description: Applied update_transaction_rewards_3847 to all 10 transactions while their cash back disputes were only SUBMITTED, not resolved or approved, contrary to doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_004.

root_cause: The agent read the 'Applying Resolved Cash Back Dispute Corrections' procedure as permission to apply its own recalculated values right after submission. It ignored the precondition that a dispute must be resolved and approved, even though its lookup showed no approved disputes.
key_facts_for_grader: The audit itself was correct: 10 errors (5 under, 5 over), none on Diamond Elite, net -17,743 points
All 10 disputes were correctly submitted by the customer via submit_cash_back_dispute_0589 and were in SUBMITTED/queued status
update_transaction_rewards_3847 may only be used after a cash back dispute is resolved and approved (doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_004)
At tool_call_60 through tool_call_69 the agent applied 10 reward updates with no approved dispute, which is an unauthorized action
The benchmark DB reward of 1 does not reflect this violation
acceptable_variations: A judge may cite tool_call_59 (unlocking update_transaction_rewards_3847) as the first critical point; tool_call_60 through tool_call_69 is where the state change occurred
A judge may additionally flag assistant_msg_5's promise to apply the values as misinformation
adjudicator_notes: The DB reward is 1 despite 10 extra writes. The DB hash probably did not cover rewards_earned changes, or the updates happened to match the expected end state. Either way, the policy precondition (resolved and approved dispute) was clearly unmet: the disputes were only SUBMITTED and the agent's own lookup at tool_result_56 found none. The audit content matches the other trace on this task.

customer_requests.request: Audit all credit card transactions across the four cards and identify every rewards error (over- and under-credits), then get them corrected
customer_requests.correct_handling: Verify (2 of DOB/email/phone/address) and log verification. Apply the earn rates: Diamond Elite 5%; Business Platinum 4% on travel/software/media-advertising and 1.5% otherwise; Business Silver 10% on travel/software and 1% otherwise, with Dell excluded; EcoCard 5x green and 1x otherwise, with Target/ThredUp excluded. Floor rewards. The 10 errors are: Patagonia txn_8a8873edaac2 (562->937), Southwest txn_4d2b795c6f98 (1,651->4,127), Google Ads txn_508e275e27af (1,875->5,000), Marriott Bonvoy txn_30cb41175311 (10,684->5,342), REI Co-op txn_f84fa27a1b54 (234->1,172), Facebook Ads txn_1a4918670323 (8,753->3,501), Dell txn_ffeede5eeacd (18,499->1,849), Datadog txn_097c072e7df3 (387->3,870), ThredUp txn_4f5e249acc6c (391->78), Target Eco Collection txn_ba8b473f295d (728->145). customer_requests.agent_handling: Verified with DOB and phone and logged it ([tool_call_4]-[tool_call_6]). key_facts_for_grader: Exactly 10 errors exist: 5 under-credited (Patagonia 09/16, Southwest 09/17, Google Ads 09/21, REI Co-op 09/24, Datadog 10/10) and 5 over-credited (Marriott Bonvoy 09/23, Facebook Ads 09/29, Dell 10/05, ThredUp 10/12, Target Eco Collection 10/16); no Diamond Elite errors

Net correction is -17,743 points
acceptable_variations: Granting the tool 10 times (once per transaction) is harmless
Walking the customer through one submission at a time is acceptable
The JSON-formatted assistant messages are a style issue, not an error
adjudicator_notes: All 10 gold dispute submissions matched. Task notes mention 75 transactions while the DB returned 77; this is irrelevant to correctness.

She then applied for the Diamond Elite Card herself.

customer_requests.request: Check whether she qualifies for the Platinum Rewards Card annual-fee rebate based on her spending history
customer_requests.correct_handling: Verify identity and log it. Apply doc_credit_cards_platinum_rewards_card_010: at least $7,500 in posted net purchases in each of the 12 monthly anniversary windows (10th to 9th inclusive). Totals: $7,594.18, $7,635.92, $7,721.49, $7,763.29, $7,845.26, $7,873.15, $7,713.77, $7,598.04, $7,601.91, $7,617.16, $7,917.61, $7,672.23. All meet the threshold, so she qualifies for the $150 rebate, credited as a statement credit after the annual fee is billed.
customer_requests.agent_handling: Verified and logged ([tool_call_4]-[tool_call_6]). At [assistant_msg_3] it presented all 12 window totals, matching the correct values exactly. It concluded she qualifies for the $150 rebate and said the rebate is applied as a statement credit after the annual fee is billed.

The lowest windows are Nov 10-Dec 9 at $7,594.18 and Jun 10-Jul 9 at $7,598.04
Identity was verified with DOB and address and logged before account lookups

A judge may note that the agent did not respond after the customer's Diamond Elite application message; the conversation ended there

summary: Marcus Chen runs a landscaping company. He wanted one new business credit card that gives the most money back on a single $40,000 work-truck purchase, and he asked the agent for one clear recommendation. The agent recommended the Silver Zoom Card ($1,200 from the triple-cash-back promo minus the $74.50 fee = $1,125.50) [assistant_msg_4][assistant_msg_5]. That card is designed for, and underwritten as, a card for established transportation and logistics businesses. The customer applied for the Silver Zoom Card instead of the Business Bronze Rewards Card ($400 cash back + $500 new-customer credit = $900, $0 fee).

customer_requests.request: Recommend the single business credit card with the highest total return on a $40,000 truck purchase for a landscaping business (no Rho-Bank+ subscription), so the customer can apply for it
customer_requests.correct_handling: Recommend the Business Bronze Rewards Card. It earns 1% cash back ($400) plus the new-customer promo (window 2025-10-01 to 2026-03-31): $10,000 in net purchases within the first 2 months earns a $500 statement credit. The total is $900 with a $0 annual fee. The Business Silver Rewards Card's 2x promo (window ends 2025-11-14) gives 2% = $800, but its first-year fee waiver window only starts 2025-11-15, so the net is $677.50. Platinum earns 1.5% = $600 and Gold earns 1% less a $200 fee. The Silver Zoom Card is designed for established transportation and logistics operators, and its eligibility doc frames approval as 'for logistics business approval'. It is not the right product for a landscaping company. Then let the customer apply with card_type 'Business Bronze Rewards Card', annual_income 120000, rho_bank_subscription false.
customer_requests.agent_handling: At [assistant_msg_4] the agent ranked the Silver Zoom Card first and said its fleet perks 'fit landscaping'. It ranked Business Bronze ($900) second. When asked for one recommendation at [user_msg_2], the agent gave only the Silver Zoom Card at [assistant_msg_5], quoting a net of $1,125.50 (3% x $40,000 = $1,200 minus the $74.50 fee). It never addressed the fact that Silver Zoom is built for transportation and logistics operators. The customer applied for the Silver Zoom Card.

errors.finding: The agent presented the Silver Zoom Card as the 'best overall return' for a landscaping business and said its fleet perks fit landscaping. The KB describes Silver Zoom as 'Designed for Transportation and Logistics Businesses' for 'established transportation and logistics operators', and its eligibility is framed 'for logistics business approval'. The correct recommendation was the Business Bronze Rewards Card ($400 + $500 credit = $900, $0 fee).

The customer asked for one clear recommendation. The agent gave only the Silver Zoom Card (claimed net $1,125.50), and the customer applied for it. The single correct recommendation was the Business Bronze Rewards Card with a $900 total return.

first_critical_error.description: Recommended the Silver Zoom Card, a card for transportation and logistics operators, to a landscaping business as the best option, instead of the Business Bronze Rewards Card ($900 total, $0 fee). The single recommendation at assistant_msg_5 confirmed this.

root_cause: The agent found the Silver Zoom triple-cash-back promo (3x1% = 3%) and optimized purely on arithmetic. It ignored the card's stated target market of established transportation and logistics businesses, which a landscaping company is not.
key_facts_for_grader: The customer is a landscaping company, not a transportation or logistics business, with a $40,000 truck purchase and no Rho-Bank+ subscription
Business Bronze Rewards Card: 1% = $400, plus a $500 statement credit for $10,000 spent in the first 2 months (promo 2025-10-01 to 2026-03-31), $0 fee, $900 total
Business Silver Rewards Card: the 2x promo ends 2025-11-14 and the fee waiver starts 2025-11-15, so the net is $800 - $122.50 = $677.50, which is less than Bronze
Silver Zoom Card is designed for established transportation and logistics operators (eligibility framed 'for logistics business approval'), so it is not the right recommendation for this customer
The agent recommended the Silver Zoom Card at assistant_msg_4/assistant_msg_5 and the customer applied for it; the correct card was the Business Bronze Rewards Card
acceptable_variations: A judge might argue the KB does not explicitly bar non-logistics businesses from Silver Zoom. A judge that flags the industry mismatch as the core problem is correct. A judge that passes the trace because of the $1,125.50 arithmetic is not consistent with this gold.
Noting that a $40,000 charge may exceed Bronze's $10,000-$50,000 line is reasonable and is not an error
adjudicator_notes: Agrees with the benchmark gold (Business Bronze) and DB reward 0. The Silver Zoom triple promo (claim window 2024-01-01 to 2025-12-31, 3x the 1% base) arithmetically beats Bronze, and the KB does not contain an explicit 'logistics businesses only' prohibition. The product is clearly positioned and underwritten for transportation and logistics operators, though, and a parallel trace (gpt-5.6-sol t2) correctly reasoned this way. Confidence is therefore medium rather than high.

summary: Sarah Mitchell runs a software company. She wanted the one new business credit card with the highest return on a single $100,000 company-wide Apple Music subscription. At [assistant_msg_2] the agent correctly identified Business Platinum's 4% software/media rate ($4,000, first-year fee waived) and that Apple is excluded from Business Silver's 10% software rate. When asked for one recommendation at [assistant_msg_3], though, it recommended the Business Silver Rewards Card ($2,000 under the double-cash promo ending that day, or $1,877.50 after the fee). The customer applied for Business Silver instead of Business Platinum.

customer_requests.request: Recommend the single business credit card with the highest total return on a $100,000 Apple Music subscription purchase (no Rho-Bank+), with the math, so the customer can apply
customer_requests.correct_handling: Recommend the Business Platinum Rewards Card. It earns 4.0% on travel, software and media purchases, including SaaS and enterprise subscriptions, and has no Apple exclusion, so $100,000 earns $4,000. The $450 annual fee is waived in the first year for accounts opened 2025-11-01 to 2026-02-28, so the net is $4,000. Business Silver explicitly excludes Apple from its 10% software rate, so it earns 1%, or 2% under the double-cash promo ending 2025-11-14: $2,000 minus the $122.50 fee (the waiver window starts 2025-11-15) = $1,877.50. Business Bronze gives $1,000 + $500 = $1,500 and its line maxes at $50,000. The customer applies with card_type 'Business Platinum Rewards Card', income 250000, rho_bank_subscription false.
customer_requests.agent_handling: At [assistant_msg_2] the agent listed Platinum as the 'best general choice' (4% = $4,000, or 1.5% = $1,500). It treated Apple Music's software/media coding as uncertain. At [assistant_msg_3] it recommended the Business Silver Rewards Card as the 'reliable' choice: 2% = $2,000, or a conservative $1,877.50 net after the $122.50 fee. It said Platinum wins only if Apple confirms eligible coding. The customer applied for Business Silver.

errors.finding: The customer asked for one card. The agent recommended the Business Silver Rewards Card ($2,000 gross / $1,877.50 net) instead of the Business Platinum Rewards Card. Platinum earns 4.0% on software and media subscriptions with no Apple exclusion, and its first-year fee is waived, for a net of $4,000. The agent also used probability-of-coding reasoning (Platinum wins only if p > 15.1%) to downgrade Platinum. The KB treats Apple as a software merchant: Business Silver excludes it specifically as a 'Software Exclusion', and Platinum has no such exclusion.

first_critical_error.description: Recommended the Business Silver Rewards Card ($2,000 / $1,877.50) as the single card instead of the Business Platinum Rewards Card (4% = $4,000, first-year fee $0).

root_cause: The agent treated Platinum's 4% on an Apple Music subscription as speculative merchant-coding risk and chose the 'guaranteed' 2% promo on Business Silver. The KB itself classifies Apple purchases as software (Silver's exclusion list), and Platinum carries no Apple exclusion.
key_facts_for_grader: Correct card: Business Platinum Rewards Card, 4% on software/media = $4,000 on $100,000, with the first-year $450 fee waived (promo 2025-11-01 to 2026-02-28), net $4,000
Business Silver excludes Apple from its 10% software rate, so it earns 1%, or 2% under the double-cash promo ending 2025-11-14 = $2,000, minus the $122.50 fee (waiver starts 2025-11-15) = $1,877.50
Business Bronze: 1% + $500 = $1,500, and the max line of $50,000 cannot cover the charge
The agent recommended Business Silver at assistant_msg_3 and the customer applied for Business Silver; this is a wrong recommendation
acceptable_variations: A judge may treat the assistant_msg_2 table as accurate and locate the error only at assistant_msg_3's single recommendation
A judge may note that merchant-category coding risk is a legitimate caveat, but recommending Silver over Platinum on that basis is still wrong per the benchmark design and KB
Not flagging that the customer's first application used the invalid card_type 'Business Silver Rewards' (a hidden customer-side mistake) is fine
adjudicator_notes: Agrees with the benchmark gold (Business Platinum) and DB reward 0. The customer's first apply call used the invalid card_type 'Business Silver Rewards', then she retried successfully with 'Business Silver Rewards Card'. That is a customer-side mistake and not the agent's fault. Confidence is medium because the KB does not explicitly state that an Apple Music subscription codes as software or media. The intended design is clear, though: Silver's Apple 'Software Exclusion' versus no exclusion on Platinum. The agent's own fee-waiver timing analysis for Silver was correct.

summary: Sarah Mitchell runs a software company. She wanted the new business credit card with the highest return on a single $100,000 Apple Music subscription. At [assistant_msg_2] the agent compared all business cards. It noted that Apple is excluded from Business Silver's 10% software rate, and it recommended the Business Platinum Rewards Card: 4% = $4,000 if coded as software/media (1.5% = $1,500 otherwise), with the first-year fee waived. It confirmed the math at [assistant_msg_3]. The customer applied for the Business Platinum Rewards Card.

customer_requests.request: Recommend the single business credit card with the highest total return on a $100,000 Apple Music subscription purchase (no Rho-Bank+), with the math, so the customer can apply
customer_requests.correct_handling: Recommend the Business Platinum Rewards Card. It earns 4.0% on software and media with no Apple exclusion, so the purchase earns $4,000. The first-year $450 fee is waived (promo 2025-11-01 to 2026-02-28), for a net of $4,000. Business Silver excludes Apple from its 10% software rate, so it earns at most 2% = $2,000 under the double-cash promo ending 2025-11-14, less the $122.50 fee. Business Bronze gives $1,500 and its line maxes at $50,000. The customer applies with card_type 'Business Platinum Rewards Card'.
customer_requests.agent_handling: At [assistant_msg_2] the agent recommended the Business Platinum Rewards Card. It gave 4% = $4,000 (or 1.5% = $1,500 if coded otherwise), the first-year fee waived for accounts opened Nov 1, 2025 to Feb 28, 2026, and the 765 FICO / 77 PAYDEX requirements. It correctly flagged the Apple exclusion on Business Silver, Bronze's $50,000 max line, and Silver Zoom's logistics-only positioning. At [assistant_msg_3] it confirmed the $1,500 to $4,000 net and gave application guidance. The customer applied for Business Platinum.

key_facts_for_grader: Correct card: Business Platinum Rewards Card, 4% on software/media = $4,000 on $100,000, first-year fee $0 (promo 2025-11-01 to 2026-02-28)
Apple is explicitly excluded from Business Silver's 10% software rate (doc_business_credit_cards_business_silver_rewards_card_005)
The agent recommended Business Platinum and the customer applied for it with income 250000 and no Rho-Bank+
apply_for_credit_card is a customer-side tool and no KB discoverable tool exists for card applications, so no give_discoverable_user_tool call was needed
acceptable_variations: A judge may note that the agent hedged the return as $1,500-$4,000 rather than committing to $4,000. This is a cautious caveat about merchant coding, not an error, because the recommended card is correct.
A judge may flag the offer to connect a 'commercial lending specialist' as unnecessary; it is harmless
adjudicator_notes: Matches the benchmark gold and DB reward 1. No critical issues found.

summary: Amara Okonkwo holds a Business Silver Rewards Card and a personal Silver Rewards Card. She asked the agent to investigate cash back discrepancies and fix them. The agent verified her correctly and found three under-credited Business Silver transactions: JetBlue, Southwest and Zoom. It gave her the dispute tool and, after the disputes resolved, corrected those three to 6,300, 3,800 and 1,499 points. It missed the personal Silver Rewards Card's GitHub Enterprise charge ($255.00, 05/18/2025, txn_b7e2d4c5f506). That charge was credited 2,550 points (10%) instead of the card's 4% (1,020 points). The agent told the customer the personal card 'checks out', so that discrepancy was never disputed or corrected.

customer_requests.request: Verify identity and investigate cash back discrepancies across the Business Silver Rewards Card and the Silver Rewards Card
customer_requests.correct_handling: Verify with 2 of DOB/phone/email/address and log the verification. Pull the transactions and recalculate each one: Business Silver earns 10% on travel/software and 1% otherwise, with the Double Cash Back promo (2x on all purchases for 6 months from account opening on 02/13/2025, i.e. through 08/13/2025) and Apple/Microsoft/Dell/Coursera and similar merchants excluded from 10%. Silver Rewards earns 4% on travel/software and 1% otherwise. Points floor to whole numbers. Discrepancies: JetBlue $315.00 03/22/2025 (txn_a8f1c2d3e403) got 3,150 and should get 6,300 (20%). Southwest $380.00 08/25/2025 (txn_a8f1c2d3e410) got 1,520 and should get 3,800 (10%). Zoom Video $149.99 09/15/2025 (txn_a8f1c2d3e411) got 600 and should get 1,499 (10%, floored). GitHub Enterprise $255.00 05/18/2025 on the Silver Rewards Card (txn_b7e2d4c5f506) got 2,550 and should get 1,020 (4%).
customer_requests.agent_handling: The agent verified with DOB + phone and logged the verification [tool_call_7]. It correctly identified JetBlue, Southwest and Zoom [assistant_msg_9]. It stated that all 12 Silver Rewards Card transactions 'earned correctly at 4% / 1%', which missed GitHub Enterprise, credited at 10% (2,550 vs 1,020).

customer_requests.request: Help submit cash back disputes for the incorrect transactions
customer_requests.correct_handling: Give submit_cash_back_dispute_0589 and instruct the customer to submit it with user_id 755bcb4d5d for each of the four transactions: txn_a8f1c2d3e403, txn_a8f1c2d3e410, txn_a8f1c2d3e411 and txn_b7e2d4c5f506.
customer_requests.agent_handling: The agent gave the tool [assistant_msg_8] and instructed disputes for only three transactions (e403, e410, e411) [assistant_msg_9]. GitHub Enterprise (txn_b7e2d4c5f506) was never disputed.

customer_requests.request: After the disputes resolved, update the transaction records with the correct cash back
customer_requests.correct_handling: Unlock update_transaction_rewards_3847 and set: txn_a8f1c2d3e403 to '6300 points', txn_a8f1c2d3e410 to '3800 points', txn_a8f1c2d3e411 to '1499 points' (floor of 1,499.9 per the rounding policy), and txn_b7e2d4c5f506 to '1020 points' (if disputed). Confirm in the transaction history.
customer_requests.agent_handling: The agent unlocked update_transaction_rewards_3847 [tool_call_27] and set e403 to 6300, e410 to 3800 and e411 to 1499 points [tool_call_32]. It confirmed the changes via the transaction history [tool_call_33]. It did not correct GitHub Enterprise.

errors.finding: The agent told the customer that all 12 personal Silver Rewards Card transactions 'checks out' at 4%/1%. GitHub Enterprise ($255.00, 05/18/2025, Software, txn_b7e2d4c5f506) was credited 2,550 points (10%), but the Silver Rewards Card earns 4% on software, so it should be 1,020 points. The discrepancy was neither disclosed nor disputed, and the customer received dispute instructions for only 3 of the 4 incorrect transactions.

The agent said that transactions credited 'a point or two above' the correct amount are in the customer's favor and 'we won't be reducing them'. No KB policy supports this. The small rounding over-credits were not part of the expected corrections, though, so this is not counted as critical.
The rewards updates covered only e403 (6,300), e410 (3,800) and e411 (1,499). txn_b7e2d4c5f506 was never corrected to 1,020 points. The Zoom value of 1,499 is correct under the floor rounding policy.

first_critical_error.description: The agent declared the Silver Rewards Card correct and directed disputes for only 3 transactions. It missed GitHub Enterprise txn_b7e2d4c5f506 ($255.00), credited 2,550 points instead of 1,020 (4%).

root_cause: The agent audited the Silver Rewards Card looking only for under-credits. It treated over-credits as harmless and did not notice that the GitHub Enterprise charge was credited at 10%, the business card rate, instead of the personal card's 4%.
key_facts_for_grader: Verification with DOB 08/11/1997 + phone 713-555-0963 was correct and logged before account access
Business Silver Double Cash Back promo: account opened 02/13/2025, so 2x applies through 08/13/2025
GitHub Enterprise $255.00 05/18/2025 on the Silver Rewards Card (txn_b7e2d4c5f506) was credited 2,550 pts but should be 1,020 pts (4%), and the agent missed it
Only 3 of the 4 required disputes and corrections were completed
acceptable_variations: 1,499 points for Zoom is correct per the rounding (floor) policy. A judge should not flag it as wrong, even though the benchmark gold uses 1,500.
Unlocking and calling get_user_dispute_history_7291 (a transaction-dispute tool) to look for resolved cash back disputes is an extra read-only lookup and is not an error
A judge may or may not flag the 'we won't reduce small over-credits' statement
adjudicator_notes: Benchmark gold expects '1500 points' for Zoom (txn_a8f1c2d3e411). doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_007 requires flooring, so 1,499.9 becomes 1,499 and the agent's value is policy-correct; I override the gold on that argument. The DB data itself appears to round to nearest (e.g. Adobe 1,100 vs floor 1,099), which explains the gold. The fail stands on the missed GitHub Enterprise discrepancy (gold 026_3 and 026_8: 1020 points).

summary: Customer reported credit card declines despite available credit and repeatedly asked for a human. The agent gave general troubleshooting and deflected the first request [assistant_msg_3]. On the second request it called the standard transfer_to_human_agents [tool_call_3]. The KB protocol requires initial_transfer_to_human_agent_0218 for the first three requests and the standard transfer only on the fourth.

customer_requests.request: Credit card declining despite available credit; customer wants a human agent (asked at user_msg_2 and user_msg_3)
customer_requests.correct_handling: Per doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_010 (purchase declines despite available credit plus requests for a human): for the 1st, 2nd and 3rd transfer requests, unlock initial_transfer_to_human_agent_0218 and call it (tell the customer the lines are busy). Do not use transfer_to_human_agents for these requests. On the 4th request, call transfer_to_human_agents. Keep troubleshooting between requests.
customer_requests.agent_handling: Gave generic decline troubleshooting [assistant_msg_2]. On the 1st request it asked for verification instead of following the protocol [assistant_msg_3].
