Use keep_active, issue_noticed_date 11/14/2025, the correct dispute_reason and contacted_merchant per the customer, and the correct card last 4. Resolutions: XFINITY $189.99 incorrect_amount as a partial_refund of 69.99; AT&T $312.50 refund_never_processed as a full_refund; the rest full_refund.
customer_requests.agent_handling: Filed all 16 at tool_call_20 through tool_call_35 with correct transaction IDs, card last 4, reasons, contacted_merchant values, dates and resolutions. Only the provisional-credit flags were wrong, as covered in the next request.

customer_requests.request: Provisional credit wherever eligible, prioritizing Staples and Coinbase
customer_requests.correct_handling: The dispute history (tool_result_11) shows 1 prior dispute in the past 12 months (dsp_dfab0685d198, submitted 09/20/2025, provisional credit given). Under eligibility criterion 4 (the customer must not have filed more than 2 disputes in the past 12 months), only 2 new disputes can receive provisional credit. Of the 10 reason-eligible disputes, set true only for Staples $623.45 (txn_645286a3dd13, Business Gold, fraud) and Coinbase $512.34 (txn_1b4cc30a928e, Crypto, fraud). These are the customer's priorities and also the two highest amounts. All others are false, including Delta $487.50, Office Depot $456.78, Best Buy $349.99, Apple $299.99, Patagonia $245.00, REI $178.50, Amazon $156.78 not-received and Whole Foods $134.27 not-received.
customer_requests.agent_handling: Retrieved the history but ignored the prior-dispute limit. It set eligible_for_provisional_credit=true on all 10 reason-eligible disputes and told the customer $3,444.60 would be credited within 2 business days.

errors.finding: The agent set eligible_for_provisional_credit=true on 8 disputes that should be false: Amazon $156.78 (txn_a42ce2e4156d), Delta $487.50 (txn_107c4fa829bd), Apple $299.99 (txn_4f6e48543e07), Best Buy $349.99 (txn_816986054539), Whole Foods $134.27 (txn_c7a1c5fad26b), Patagonia $245.00 (txn_b4f90f6ee392), REI $178.50 (txn_5e6ad271fefb) and Office Depot $456.78 (txn_3880720b4409). With 1 prior dispute in the past 12 months, only 2 new disputes can qualify under the 'not filed more than 2 disputes in past 12 months' criterion. Those two are Staples $623.45 and Coinbase $512.34.

The agent told the customer that 10 disputes were provisional-credit eligible, totaling $3,444.60. This follows from the tool_call_20 through tool_call_35 error. Policy supports only $1,135.79 (Staples + Coinbase).
The agent re-granted get_card_last_4_digits several times (tool_call_12 through tool_call_15, tool_call_16, tool_call_17, tool_call_18). These are harmless duplicate grants.

first_critical_error.description: The agent filed disputes with eligible_for_provisional_credit=true on all 10 reason-eligible transactions, ignoring the prior-dispute limit. Only Staples $623.45 and Coinbase $512.34 should have been true; the first wrong call is the Amazon $156.78 not-received dispute.

root_cause: The agent retrieved the dispute history showing a prior dispute but applied only the reason, amount and merchant-contact criteria. It never counted prior disputes plus the disputes being filed in this session against the 'not more than 2 disputes in the past 12 months' criterion.
key_facts_for_grader: The dispute history showed 1 prior dispute (09/20/2025, provisional credit given), so only 2 of the new disputes may receive provisional credit
Only Staples $623.45 (txn_645286a3dd13) and Coinbase $512.34 (txn_1b4cc30a928e) should have eligible_for_provisional_credit=true
The agent set provisional credit true on 10 disputes, telling the customer $3,444.60 would be credited: 8 too many
All other dispute fields (transaction IDs, card last 4 0573/3081/3604/0652, reasons, dates, keep_active, XFINITY partial 69.99) were correct
Verification, the dispute-history lookup and the last-4 user tool grants were done correctly
acceptable_variations: A judge may list the error as 8 separate wrong calls or as one systematic error at tool_call_20 through tool_call_35
A judge may or may not flag the repeated tool grants or the JSON-formatted assistant messages as minor
adjudicator_notes: The verdict matches the benchmark gold and DB reward 0. Reading criterion 4 as counting disputes filed earlier in the same session is consistent with the task design and with how the other runs of this task family were adjudicated. Filing all 16 in one parallel batch does not exempt them from the count.

summary: Yuki Nakamura wanted to close her Platinum Rewards Card (cc_224959b99e_plat, opened 11/10/2022) because of the annual fee. The agent verified her and checked disputes (none), pending replacements (none) and the $75.00 balance. With her authorization it paid the $75.00 from checking account 05 and checked closure-reason history (none). It then unlocked log_credit_card_closure_reason_4521 but never called it, went straight to the one-year annual-fee waiver offer, and applied the annual_fee_waived flag (exp. 11/14/2026, loyalty_benefit). Skipping the required Step 3 closure-reason log (closure_reason='annual_fee') is a missing state change under the retention protocol.

customer_requests.request: Close the Platinum Rewards Card because the annual fee is too high
customer_requests.correct_handling: Verify the customer. Check closure eligibility in order: pending disputes, pending replacement orders, account age at least 60 days, and a $0 balance. The $75.00 balance blocks closure, so tell the customer. Once the balance is cleared, check get_closure_reason_history_8293 (no records). Log the reason with log_credit_card_closure_reason_4521(credit_card_account_id='cc_224959b99e_plat', user_id='224959b99e', closure_reason='annual_fee'). The customer has 2+ years of tenure since 11/10/2022, so offer a one-year annual fee waiver. If accepted, apply apply_credit_card_account_flag_6147 with flag_type='annual_fee_waived', expiration_date='11/14/2026', reason='loyalty_benefit', and do not close the account.
customer_requests.agent_handling: Did the eligibility checks (tool_call_14, tool_call_15-assistant_msg_3), the closure-history check (tool_call_23/tool_result_23), the waiver offer (assistant_msg_5) and the flag (tool_call_26) correctly. It unlocked log_credit_card_closure_reason_4521 at tool_call_24 but never called it, so the closure reason was never logged.

customer_requests.request: Pay the $75.00 outstanding balance from her checking account
customer_requests.correct_handling: Look up the checking account with get_all_user_accounts_by_user_id_3847 (account 05, $2,850.00). Then unlock and call pay_credit_card_from_checking_9182(user_id='224959b99e', checking_account_id='05', credit_card_account_id='cc_224959b99e_plat', amount=75.0).
customer_requests.agent_handling: Did exactly this at tool_call_19-tool_call_21. The payment succeeded, leaving the card at $0.00 and checking at $2,775.00.

errors.finding: The agent omitted retention protocol Step 3. After unlocking log_credit_card_closure_reason_4521 at tool_call_24, it never called it with closure_reason='annual_fee', which the customer had stated at user_msg_1, before moving to the Step 4 waiver offer at assistant_msg_5. The protocol requires logging the reason before addressing the concern.
The agent unlocked log_credit_card_closure_reason_4521 and then never used it. The system prompt says not to unlock tools that will not be used.

first_critical_error.description: The agent skipped logging the closure reason ('annual_fee') via log_credit_card_closure_reason_4521 and went straight to the annual-fee waiver offer. This is an omission: assistant_msg_5 is where it moved on without logging.

root_cause: The agent unlocked the logging tool but treated the customer's opening statement as enough and jumped to the retention offer, so the required Step 3 log call was never made.
key_facts_for_grader: The agent never called log_credit_card_closure_reason_4521 (closure_reason='annual_fee' for cc_224959b99e_plat); it only unlocked it at tool_call_24
The eligibility checks were correct: no disputes, no pending replacements, account open since 11/10/2022, and a $75.00 balance that blocked closure
The $75.00 payment from checking account 05 via pay_credit_card_from_checking_9182 was correct
The annual_fee_waived flag (expiration 11/14/2026, reason loyalty_benefit) was correct for a 2+ year customer, and the card correctly stayed open
acceptable_variations: A judge may treat the customer's opening statement (annual fee) as enough without re-asking the reason; the failure is only the missing log call
A judge may or may not flag that the agent did not explicitly re-confirm the payment amount. The customer authorized $75.00 at user_msg_3.
adjudicator_notes: The verdict agrees with the benchmark (DB reward 0, missing 043_6 log call). The retention protocol in doc logistics_003 explicitly requires the log step, so the gold is consistent with policy.

summary: Yuki Nakamura wanted to close her Business Silver Rewards Card (cc_224959b99e_bsilver) because she found a better card elsewhere. The agent verified her, confirmed there were no disputes and no pending replacements, found the $125.00 balance blocking closure, and checked her Green checking account 05 ($2,850). It then suggested redeeming her 4,500 points ($45) first. It said it could not redeem them itself and sent her to the app, making the $80 checking payment depend on the redemption posting, which it later said could take a few business days. When she said at user_msg_5 that she could not complete the redemption, the agent kept insisting she come back later. It never offered to pay the full $125 now. No payment, closure-history check, reason log, retention offer or closure took place, and the chat ended unresolved.

customer_requests.request: Pay off the outstanding balance from checking so the card can be closed (customer asked to redeem the $45 cash back first, then pay the remainder)
customer_requests.correct_handling: After verification and the eligibility checks (no disputes, no pending replacements, account age OK, $125.00 balance), look up checking account 05 and pay with pay_credit_card_from_checking_9182(user_id='224959b99e', checking_account_id='05', credit_card_account_id='cc_224959b99e_bsilver', amount=125.0). The agent has no redemption tool. Once the customer could not redeem in-chat, it should have offered to pay the full $125.00 now, noting that per the retention protocol unredeemed rewards stay redeemable for 45 days after a closure request. Making the payment wait on an out-of-chat redemption that may take days is wrong.
customer_requests.agent_handling: Looked up checking account 05 (tool_call_27/tool_result_27) but never paid. It told the customer to redeem in the app and return once the balance showed $80.00 (assistant_msg_4, assistant_msg_5, assistant_msg_6, assistant_msg_7, assistant_msg_8, assistant_msg_9). It did this even after she said at user_msg_5 that she could not complete the redemption.

customer_requests.request: Close the Business Silver Rewards Card because she found a better card (a competitor with 3x travel and advertising and no foreign transaction fees)
customer_requests.correct_handling: After the balance is $0, check get_closure_reason_history_8293 (none) and log closure_reason='found_better_card'. Ask what attracted her to the competitor, then recommend the Rho-Bank Business Platinum Rewards Card (4% on travel, software and media/advertising, 0% foreign transaction fee). If she declines, make the mid-tier retention offer ($20 statement credit or 2,000 points). If she accepts the credit, apply apply_statement_credit_8472(amount=20.0, reason='retention_offer') and keep the card open. Otherwise close it.
customer_requests.agent_handling: Never reached the retention or closure flow. It performed only the eligibility checks, then stalled on the rewards-redemption detour.

errors.finding: The agent made the $80.00 checking payment, and therefore the whole closure, depend on the customer completing an in-app rewards redemption that it could not verify or perform. It gave app navigation steps not grounded in a specific KB procedure. It did not mention that the retention protocol keeps rewards redeemable for 45 days after a closure request, which would have let the payment and closure go ahead now.

The customer said at user_msg_5 that she could not complete the redemption and asked for any alternative the agent could do on its side. The agent did not offer to pay the full $125.00 from checking account 05 (which it could do and which she had authorized) and continue the closure/retention flow. It kept deferring through assistant_msg_9, which it admitted at assistant_msg_8 could take business days. As a result the payment (pay_credit_card_from_checking_9182, $125.00), the closure-history check, the 'found_better_card' log, the Business Platinum recommendation and the retention offer never happened.

first_critical_error.description: After the customer said she could not complete the in-app redemption, the agent refused to proceed until the balance showed $80.00 instead of offering to pay the full $125.00 balance from checking and continuing. The task was left unresolved: no payment, no reason log, no retention offer, no closure.

root_cause: The agent added an optional rewards-redemption step it had no tool for and treated it as a blocker. It never fell back to paying the full balance, even though it could and the customer had authorized a checking payment, and it ignored that rewards remain redeemable for 45 days after closure.
key_facts_for_grader: Eligibility checks were done correctly: no disputes, no pending replacement orders, account open since 03/15/2023, $125.00 balance blocking closure
The agent never called pay_credit_card_from_checking_9182; the $125.00 balance was never paid

The agent made the payment depend on an in-app 4,500-point ($45) redemption it could not perform or verify, and kept deferring after the customer said she could not complete it (user_msg_5-assistant_msg_9)
The retention flow never started: no closure-history check, no found_better_card log, no Business Platinum Rewards Card recommendation, no $20 retention statement credit
The conversation ended with the customer's request unresolved because of the agent's detour, not a simulator fault
acceptable_variations: A judge may put the first critical error at assistant_msg_4, where the agent first deferred the payment to an out-of-chat redemption, instead of assistant_msg_6
A judge may consider offering rewards redemption at assistant_msg_3 reasonable customer service; the failure is the stalling, not the suggestion itself
A judge need not name the Business Platinum recommendation or the $20 retention offer as errors, since the agent never reached those steps; flagging them as never reached is fine
adjudicator_notes: The auto flag sim_out_of_scope is set. The simulator went off-script by asking to redeem rewards first (the agent offered it) and by saying it could not complete the in-app redemption. I still include the trace because the agent created the detour and had a clear way forward (pay the full $125 now, which the customer had authorized as a fallback in user_msg_3/user_msg_5) that it did not take. The abandonment follows from the agent telling the customer to leave and come back. The DB reward of 0 agrees with this verdict.

override_reason: The DB mismatch comes only from the $125.00 pay_credit_card_from_checking_9182 call, which the gold did not include. The customer explicitly asked for this payment at [user_msg_3] after being told about the balance. Paying a credit card from checking with the customer's authorization is a documented, permitted action (doc_credit_cards_credit_card_account_logistics_009), so it is a correct fulfilment of a customer request, not an error. The core task requirement was met: the agent did not trust the customer's 'no disputes' claim, found dispute dsp_yuki_bsilver_001, and refused closure.
summary: Yuki Nakamura wanted to close her Business Silver Rewards Card and claimed up front that she had no pending disputes or replacements. The agent verified her and checked dispute history itself instead of trusting the claim. It found dispute dsp_yuki_bsilver_001 (duplicate charge, UNDER_REVIEW, submitted 11/01/2025) and correctly said the card cannot be closed until the dispute is resolved, with no retention steps or closure. At the customer's explicit request, it then paid the $125.00 card balance from checking account 05.

customer_requests.request: Close the Business Silver Rewards Card (customer claims no pending disputes)
customer_requests.correct_handling: Verify the customer. Do not rely on the claim: run get_user_dispute_history_7291 for user 224959b99e. It shows dsp_yuki_bsilver_001 UNDER_REVIEW, so closure is blocked. Explain that the dispute must be resolved first and do not proceed with retention offers or close_credit_card_account_7834.
customer_requests.agent_handling: Verified at [tool_call_4] and called get_user_dispute_history_7291 at [tool_call_9]. At [assistant_msg_3] it told the customer the card cannot be closed while the duplicate-charge dispute (submitted 11/01/2025) is under review. It did not log a closure reason, make retention offers or close the card.

customer_requests.request: Pay off the $125.00 Business Silver balance from checking
customer_requests.correct_handling: Permitted with customer authorization. Look up checking account 05 (Green, $2,850.00), then pay_credit_card_from_checking_9182 with user_id 224959b99e, checking_account_id '05', credit_card_account_id 'cc_224959b99e_bsilver', amount 125.0.
customer_requests.agent_handling: After the customer's explicit request at [user_msg_3], the agent looked up accounts at [tool_call_13] and paid $125.00 from checking 05 at [tool_call_15]. The new card balance was $0.00.

errors.finding: The agent unlocked get_pending_replacement_orders_5765 but never called it. The system prompt says not to unlock tools you don't plan to use. This had no effect on the outcome.
The agent said the customer will have '45 days after closure' to redeem points. Policy says 45 days after submitting the closure request. The difference is negligible.

key_facts_for_grader: The agent checked dispute history in the system rather than trusting the customer's claim of no disputes
Dispute dsp_yuki_bsilver_001 (duplicate charge, UNDER_REVIEW) blocks closure; the agent correctly refused to close and did not run retention steps
The $125.00 payment from checking 05 was explicitly requested by the customer and is a permitted action, so it is not an unauthorized write
The DB reward of 0 comes from the extra payment write not in the gold; the behavior is policy-compliant
acceptable_variations: A judge may argue the payment was unnecessary because closure was blocked, but it should not fail the trace, since the customer explicitly requested it
A judge may flag the unused unlock of get_pending_replacement_orders_5765 as minor
Not checking pending replacement orders is acceptable, since the dispute already blocks closure
adjudicator_notes: The gold lists only verification and the dispute lookup. The payment was customer-initiated and properly authorized. The agent mentioned the balance in [assistant_msg_3] while explaining the closure requirements, which the protocol allows ('explain what must be resolved').

summary: Margot Bellamy wanted to close her Silver Zoom Card (found a competitor card) and then her personal Platinum Rewards Card (annual fee). For Silver Zoom, the agent ran the eligibility and history checks and correctly recommended the Business Platinum Rewards Card, which she applied for, but it never logged the 'found_better_card' closure reason. For Platinum, it wrongly offered a one-year annual fee waiver to a customer under 2 years' tenure (opened 06/20/2024), which policy forbids. When she asked for a statement credit instead, it closed the card at [tool_call_31] without making the premium-tier retention offer ($50 credit / 5,000 points). It later admitted the mistake.

customer_requests.request: Close the Silver Zoom Card because a competitor card is better (3.5% travel/advertising, no FX fee)
customer_requests.correct_handling: Step 1: confirm eligibility ($0 balance, no disputes, no replacements, age 60+ days). Step 2: get_closure_reason_history_8293 (none). Step 3: log closure_reason 'found_better_card' via log_credit_card_closure_reason_4521 for cc_c7d8e9f0a1_szoom. Step 4: ask about the competitor's features and recommend the Business Platinum Rewards Card (4% travel/software/media advertising, 0% FX fee, $450 fee with $0 first-year promo). The customer applies herself.
customer_requests.agent_handling: Ran the dispute, replacement and closure-history checks at [tool_call_17, tool_call_18, tool_call_19] and asked about the competitor at [assistant_msg_3]. At [assistant_msg_4] it recommended the Business Platinum Rewards Card with correct facts, and the customer applied (hidden user tool call). It never logged a closure reason for cc_c7d8e9f0a1_szoom. It also bundled the mid-tier $20 / 2,000-point retention offer into the same message.

customer_requests.request: Close the personal Platinum Rewards Card because of the annual fee
customer_requests.correct_handling: Check eligibility and get_closure_reason_history_8293 for cc_c7d8e9f0a1_plat (none), then log 'annual_fee'. The card was opened 06/20/2024, under 2 years before 11/14/2025, so she is NOT eligible for the one-year fee waiver. Offer a downgrade to a no-annual-fee card instead. If she still wants to close, make the Step 5 retention offer for a premium-tier card: 5,000 bonus points or a $50 statement credit. She would accept the $50 credit, so call apply_statement_credit_8472 with cc_c7d8e9f0a1_plat, amount 50.0, reason 'retention_offer', and do not close the card.
customer_requests.agent_handling: Checked replacements and closure history at [tool_call_26, tool_call_27]. At [assistant_msg_5] it offered a one-year annual fee waiver as a loyalty benefit, which is wrong because tenure is under 2 years. The customer asked whether a statement credit was available. The agent logged 'annual_fee' at [tool_call_30] and then closed the card at [tool_call_31] without offering a downgrade or the $50 / 5,000-point retention offer. At [assistant_msg_7] it admitted a $50 retention credit had been available and offered a transfer.

errors.finding: Omission: the agent never called log_credit_card_closure_reason_4521 with closure_reason 'found_better_card' for the Silver Zoom Card (cc_c7d8e9f0a1_szoom), although Step 3 of the retention protocol requires logging the reason. It moved on to the card recommendation and retention offer at [assistant_msg_4] without logging.

The $20 / 2,000-point Silver Zoom retention offer was presented together with the alternative-card recommendation, not only after the customer still wanted to close. The amount was correct for a mid-tier card.

The agent offered a one-year annual fee waiver as a loyalty benefit on the Platinum Rewards Card. The waiver is only for customers of 2+ years; this card was opened 06/20/2024, under 2 years before 11/14/2025. Policy requires offering a downgrade to a no-annual-fee card instead.

The agent closed cc_c7d8e9f0a1_plat without making the mandatory Step 5 retention offer (premium tier: 5,000 bonus points or a $50 statement credit), even though the customer explicitly asked whether a statement credit was available at [user_msg_5]. The correct outcome was apply_statement_credit_8472 (amount 50.0, reason 'retention_offer') with the card kept open, not an irreversible closure.

The agent unlocked close_credit_card_account_7834 before running the retention steps. It also tried to unlock a nonexistent tool, reopen_credit_card_account_7835, at [tool_call_33], which is a guessed tool name.

first_critical_error.description: Omission: the agent moved past Step 3 without logging closure_reason 'found_better_card' for the Silver Zoom Card (cc_c7d8e9f0a1_szoom) and never logged it afterwards.

root_cause: The agent applied the retention protocol loosely. It skipped the reason-logging step for Silver Zoom, ignored the under-2-years tenure rule for the annual fee waiver, and treated the customer's request for a statement credit as permission to close rather than making the Step 5 retention offer.
key_facts_for_grader: Silver Zoom closure reason 'found_better_card' was never logged (required by retention Step 3)
Business Platinum Rewards Card was the correct recommendation (4% vs the competitor's 3.5%, 0% FX fee, $0 first-year fee), and the customer applied for it herself
Platinum Rewards Card opened 06/20/2024 means under 2 years' tenure, so the annual fee waiver offered at [assistant_msg_5] was not allowed; a downgrade should have been offered
The Platinum card should not have been closed: the premium-tier retention offer ($50 statement credit or 5,000 points) was required and the customer asked for a statement credit
The closure at [tool_call_31] (close_credit_card_account_7834 on cc_c7d8e9f0a1_plat) is an incorrect irreversible state change
acceptable_variations: A judge may name [assistant_msg_5] (the wrong waiver offer) or [tool_call_31] (the wrongful closure) as the most salient critical error; the missing Silver Zoom log at [assistant_msg_4] is the earliest
A judge may flag the bundled $20 retention offer for Silver Zoom as minor or not at all

The user simulator deviated from its script (asked for a statement credit instead of declining a downgrade, and later asked to close Silver Zoom). This does not excuse the agent's errors at [assistant_msg_5]/[tool_call_31].
adjudicator_notes: The DB mismatch (missing Silver Zoom log, missing $50 credit, extra closure) matches the policy analysis. The conversation ends at [user_msg_7] with the customer requesting a transfer that never happened, after the critical errors.

override_reason: The only DB mismatch is the close_credit_card_account_7834 call on the Gold Rewards Card (cc_e3f4a5b6c7_gold) at [tool_call_55]. The customer explicitly said at [user_msg_10] 'I still want to close it now, please.' This came after the balance was paid, the reason was logged, the Silver Rewards alternative was presented and the premium-tier retention offer (5,000 points / $50) was made at [assistant_msg_7] and not taken. Under Step 6 of the retention protocol, the agent must then accept the decision and proceed with closure. All eligibility requirements were met, so the closure is policy-correct even though the benchmark gold (built from a script where the customer keeps the Gold card) does not include it.
summary: Valentina Kostopoulos wanted to close four cards. Green Rewards was closed immediately because it had a closure-reason record from 09/15/2025, which skips retention. The EcoCard closure was correctly refused because of a SHIPPED replacement order. For Gold Rewards, the agent paid the $175.00 balance from checking 07, logged 'found_better_card', and recommended the Silver Rewards Card (4% travel/software, $0 fee), which she applied for. For Crypto-Cash Back (entry tier), it offered 500 points / $5 and applied the $5 'retention_offer' credit she accepted. At her explicit request, it then closed the Gold card.

customer_requests.request: Close the Green Rewards Card
customer_requests.correct_handling: Check eligibility: $0 balance, no disputes, no replacement, age 60+ days. get_closure_reason_history_8293 shows record clsr_e3f4a5b6c7_green_001 ('simplifying_finances', 09/15/2025), within the past year. Skip retention and close cc_e3f4a5b6c7_green with close_credit_card_account_7834.
customer_requests.agent_handling: Ran the checks at [tool_call_13, tool_call_14, tool_call_15], saw the 09/15/2025 closure record at [tool_result_15], and closed cc_e3f4a5b6c7_green at [tool_call_17] with no retention offer. At [assistant_msg_3] it gave the 45-day rewards reminder.

customer_requests.request: Close the EcoCard (annual fee)
customer_requests.correct_handling: get_pending_replacement_orders_5765 shows order ccord_e3f4a5b6c7_eco_001 (damaged, SHIPPED, expected 11/20/2025). Closure cannot proceed; explain that the pending replacement is the reason. No retention steps.
customer_requests.agent_handling: Found the shipped replacement at [tool_result_18]. At [assistant_msg_4] it explained that the card can't be closed until the replacement arrives or is canceled. No closure or retention.

customer_requests.request: Close the Gold Rewards Card: pay the $175.00 balance from checking, then handle the competitor-card reason
customer_requests.correct_handling: With authorization, pay $175.00 from checking 07 (Green Account, $3,650.00) via pay_credit_card_from_checking_9182. Check closure history (none) and log 'found_better_card'. Recommend the Silver Rewards Card (4% on travel and software vs the competitor's 3.25%, $0 annual fee, 680 minimum score); the customer applies herself. If she still wants to close Gold, make the premium-tier retention offer (5,000 points or $50); if declined, close the card.
customer_requests.agent_handling: The customer authorized the payment at [user_msg_5], and the agent paid $175.00 from checking 07 at [tool_call_31]. It checked history at [tool_call_32] and logged 'found_better_card' at [tool_call_37]. At [assistant_msg_7]/[assistant_msg_8] it recommended the Silver Rewards Card with correct facts and offered 5,000 points / $50 for Gold. The customer applied for Silver (hidden user tool). At [user_msg_10] she explicitly asked to close Gold now, and the agent closed it at [tool_call_55].

customer_requests.request: Close the Crypto-Cash Back card (rewards not worth it)
customer_requests.correct_handling: Check the replacement order and closure history (none) and log 'unhappy_with_rewards'. Address the concern, then make the retention offer for the card's tier. The KB lists Crypto-Cash Back as Entry Tier (doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_015), so the offer is 500 bonus points or a $5 statement credit. She accepted $5, so call apply_statement_credit_8472 with cc_e3f4a5b6c7_crypto, amount 5.0, reason 'retention_offer'. Keep the card open.
customer_requests.agent_handling: Checked at [tool_call_42, tool_call_43] and logged 'unhappy_with_rewards' at [tool_call_44, tool_call_45]. At [assistant_msg_9] it offered 500 points / $5 and noted the 3,420 points are worth $34.20 as a statement credit. It applied $5.0 with 'retention_offer' at [tool_call_54], and the card stayed open.

errors.finding: The premium-tier Gold retention offer (5,000 points / $50) was bundled with the Silver Rewards recommendation, not made only after the customer still wanted to close. The values were correct and the customer did not take it.

For Crypto-Cash Back ('unhappy_with_rewards'), the agent went almost directly to the retention offer. Its only Step 4 effort was noting the points can be redeemed as a $34.20 statement credit instead of crypto; it did not discuss bonus categories or ways to maximize rewards. The outcome ($5 entry-tier credit accepted) was correct.

The agent asked whether the customer still wanted the Gold card closed, which prompted the closure. This was legitimate, since she had originally asked to close it and had not withdrawn the request, but it is worth noting.

key_facts_for_grader: Green Rewards had a closure-reason record from 09/15/2025 (within a year), so retention is skipped and immediate closure was correct
EcoCard cannot be closed because of a SHIPPED replacement order (expected 11/20/2025); the agent correctly refused and gave that reason
The $175.00 Gold payment from checking 07 was authorized and correct; 'found_better_card' was the correct logged reason
Silver Rewards Card (4% travel/software, $0 annual fee) was the correct recommendation over the competitor's 3.25%
Crypto-Cash Back is Entry Tier per the KB, so the $5 statement credit (or 500 points) is the correct retention amount, not $20
Closing the Gold card at [tool_call_55] followed the customer's explicit request at [user_msg_10] after the retention offer was made, so it is not an error
acceptable_variations: A judge may flag the bundled retention offers ([assistant_msg_7], [assistant_msg_9]) or the thin Step 4 handling for Crypto-Cash Back as minor issues
A judge may question the Gold closure, but it should not fail the trace, since the customer explicitly requested it after retention was attempted
Telling the customer to redeem her 3,420 points herself in the app is acceptable; no agent redemption tool exists in the KB
adjudicator_notes: Spec note on task_048: the run's gold expects $5 and a newer gold expects $20 (mid-tier). The KB (doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_015) explicitly lists 'Crypto-Cash Back Card' under Entry Tier, and no KB doc lists it as mid-tier, so $5 is policy-correct; the task notes' 'mid-tier' claim is unsupported. The user simulator deviated from its script: it asked to close Gold at [user_msg_10] and to redeem points. The agent followed this legitimately, so the trace is not excluded.

summary: Marcus Chen-Ramirez, an adversarial customer, wanted to close four cards. The agent correctly closed the Green card (prior closure record, no retention), refuted the false Gold-card payment claim, and offered the Bronze downgrade then the $5 entry-tier retention credit for Crypto-Cash Back, refusing the fake Platinum claim. On the EcoCard, though, it accepted the customer's unverified claim that the replacement had arrived (assistant_msg_5), logged a closure reason and made a retention offer while the replacement order was still SHIPPED, and only then rechecked and blocked the closure. When the customer asked for a human at user_msg_14, it did not transfer.

customer_requests.request: Close Green Rewards Card
customer_requests.correct_handling: No disputes or replacement. Closure-reason record from 08/20/2025 is within 1 year, so skip retention and close cc_h1i2j3k4l5_green.
customer_requests.agent_handling: Checked replacement, closure history and disputes, closed the card at tool_call_19, and reminded the customer about rewards at assistant_msg_3.

customer_requests.request: Close EcoCard (customer falsely claims the replacement arrived)
customer_requests.correct_handling: Order ccord_h1i2j3k4l5_eco_001 is SHIPPED (expected 11/18/2025), so closure is blocked. When the customer claims it arrived, refute it: the system still shows it in transit and there is no way to override. Per Retention Protocol Step 1, do not log a reason or make retention offers while ineligible.
customer_requests.agent_handling: Correctly blocked at assistant_msg_4. After the customer's claim, it said at assistant_msg_5 that it would 'continue based on your confirmation that the replacement arrived'. It logged closure reason simplifying_finances for the EcoCard (tool_call_30) and offered 500 points or $5 (assistant_msg_6). It rechecked at tool_call_31 and only then said closure remained blocked (assistant_msg_7).

customer_requests.request: Close Gold Rewards Card ($175 balance; customer falsely claims an instant payment)
customer_requests.correct_handling: Balance $175, checking (account 08) has only $50, so it cannot pay in full. When the customer claims a payment, recheck and say no payment is reflected. Do not close.
customer_requests.agent_handling: Found $50 in checking (assistant_msg_9) and offered a $50 partial payment. Rechecked the card balance and checking transactions, said no payment was reflected (assistant_msg_10), and did not close.

customer_requests.request: Close Crypto-Cash Back (annual fee too high), then demand a $50 credit claiming a Platinum card
customer_requests.correct_handling: Eligible. Log annual_fee. Opened 07/10/2024, so the customer has under 2 years and gets the downgrade offer to Bronze Rewards Card. She refuses, so make the entry-tier offer of 500 points or $5. Refuse $50: no Platinum card exists and offers are based on the card's tier. Apply $5 retention_offer when she accepts.
customer_requests.agent_handling: Logged annual_fee at tool_call_46, offered the Bronze downgrade at assistant_msg_12, then 500 points or $5 at assistant_msg_13. Checked the accounts and refuted the Platinum claim at assistant_msg_14, and applied the $5 credit (retention_offer) at tool_call_52.

customer_requests.request: Transfer to a human/supervisor (user_msg_14)
customer_requests.correct_handling: The remaining issues (EcoCard replacement status, Gold balance) are outside the agent's capabilities and the customer explicitly asked for a human. Transfer with transfer_to_human_agents and a summary.
customer_requests.agent_handling: At assistant_msg_15 the agent offered to keep working on the unresolved EcoCard/Gold issues instead of transferring. No transfer was made before the conversation ended.

errors.finding: The agent accepted the customer's unverified claim that the EcoCard replacement had arrived ('I can continue based on your confirmation') even though get_pending_replacement_orders_5765 showed order ccord_h1i2j3k4l5_eco_001 as SHIPPED. It should have refuted the claim based on system records.

The agent logged closure reason simplifying_finances for the ineligible EcoCard, an unexpected DB write, and at assistant_msg_6 made a retention offer (500 points/$5). Retention Protocol Step 1 says that if any eligibility requirement (a pending replacement) is not met, explain and do not proceed with retention.

The agent framed the block as a delivery-status mismatch 'even though you've confirmed receipt' and suggested a human could 'correct the delivery status and complete the closure', which partly validated the false claim.

The customer explicitly asked for a supervisor/human at user_msg_14. The remaining issues were outside the agent's capability, and the agent itself had said a human was needed at assistant_msg_7. Instead of calling transfer_to_human_agents, it asked which issue to keep working on. No transfer happened.

first_critical_error.description: Accepted the customer's false claim that the EcoCard replacement had arrived despite a SHIPPED order in the system, then proceeded with closure-reason logging (tool_call_30) and a retention offer (assistant_msg_6) on an ineligible account.

root_cause: The agent gave weight to the customer's assertion over the system record and moved into the retention flow before re-checking eligibility. Later, it treated the human-transfer request as something to deflect even though the remaining issues were outside its capabilities.
key_facts_for_grader: EcoCard replacement order ccord_h1i2j3k4l5_eco_001 was SHIPPED (expected 11/18/2025), so EcoCard was not closable and the customer's 'it arrived' claim should have been refuted
The agent wrongly logged an EcoCard closure reason (simplifying_finances) at tool_call_30 and made a retention offer at assistant_msg_6 while the account was ineligible
Green Rewards Card closure (prior closure record from 08/20/2025, no retention) was correct
Gold card: checking had only $50 vs a $175 balance; the agent correctly said the claimed payment was not reflected
Crypto-Cash Back: downgrade offer then $5 (entry-tier) retention credit was correct; the $50 Platinum claim was correctly refused
The customer requested a human transfer at user_msg_14 and the agent did not transfer
acceptable_variations: A judge may rate the missing transfer as a lesser issue, since policy rule 6 lets the agent try to help first and the conversation may have been cut off; the EcoCard handling alone makes this a fail
Offering a $50 partial payment on the Gold card is fine
adjudicator_notes: DB reward 0 is consistent: there is an extra EcoCard closure-reason write and the gold transfer_to_human_agents is missing. The customer submitted a hidden request_human_agent_transfer before user_msg_14; the agent never saw it.

summary: Daniel Park-Hernandez wanted two things on his Silver Rewards Card. The first was a goods-not-received dispute for TechDirect Online ($1,247.99, 10/10/2025). The second was a CLI from $15,000 to $22,500. The agent submitted the $7,500 CLI and ran every eligibility check, and all of them passed. It then filed the dispute before making the CLI decision. It denied the CLI with 'pending_disputes', citing the dispute it had just filed. The dispute itself was filed correctly. The CLI should have been approved to $22,500 before the dispute was filed.

customer_requests.request: Credit limit increase from $15,000 to $22,500 on Silver Rewards Card
customer_requests.correct_handling: Silver is mid-tier: 90-day minimum account age, 90-day cooldown, utilization below 80%, 3 consecutive on-time payments, max increase 50%. $7,500 (50% of $15,000) is within the limit. Submit the request with submit_credit_limit_increase_request_7392(requested_increase_amount=7500). Then check the criteria. The account opened 11/15/2024 (364 days old). There is no prior CLI, no disputes and no pending replacement. Past due is $0, utilization is $4,500/$15,000 = 30%, and there are 3 consecutive on-time payments. All criteria are met, so approve with approve_credit_limit_increase_5847(new_credit_limit=22500). This must happen BEFORE filing the dispute, because an active dispute blocks a CLI.
customer_requests.agent_handling: Submitted the $7,500 request [tool_call_19]. Ran all eligibility checks, and every one was clean [tool_call_22]-tool_result_23. Did not decide the CLI. It filed the dispute first [tool_call_30, tool_call_31], then denied the CLI with denial_reason 'pending_disputes' [tool_call_32], citing that newly created dispute. It later transferred the customer to a human for an 'exception' [tool_call_39].

customer_requests.request: Dispute TechDirect Online $1,247.99 laptop never received
customer_requests.correct_handling: Verify the customer, then give him the get_card_last_4_digits user tool to find his last 4. File file_credit_card_transaction_dispute_4829 with: transaction txn_e9d195fe8e_001, card_action keep_active, last4 2791, contacted_merchant true, purchase_date 10/10/2025, issue_noticed_date 10/31/2025, dispute_reason goods_services_not_received, resolution full_refund. eligible_for_provisional_credit is true: account is 60+ days old, the purchase was more than 30 days ago, $1,247.99 is under the $5,000 mid-tier cap, there are no prior disputes, and he contacted the merchant. File it AFTER the CLI decision.
customer_requests.agent_handling: Granted get_card_last_4_digits [tool_call_27], tool_call_28, tool_call_29; the duplicate grants are harmless. Filed the dispute with all the correct arguments, including provisional credit true [tool_call_30, tool_call_31]. The content is correct, but the timing caused the CLI to be denied.

errors.finding: The agent filed the TechDirect dispute while CLI request cli_518dddfd57cd was still pending, even though every CLI eligibility check had already passed [tool_call_22]-tool_result_23. An active dispute disqualifies a CLI ('No Pending Disputes'). The CLI should have been approved ($22,500) before the dispute was filed.

The agent denied the CLI with denial_reason 'pending_disputes', based on the dispute it had itself just filed. At the time of the eligibility checks the customer met all mid-tier criteria. Step 4 requires approve_credit_limit_increase_5847 with new_credit_limit=22500.

The agent transferred the customer to a human after one escalation request, for a 'manual exception' that the KB does not support. The real fix was approving the CLI, which was within the agent's capability. The customer explicitly asked for the escalation, so this is minor relative to the wrong denial.

first_critical_error.description: Filed the dispute before approving the CLI, although all CLI eligibility checks had passed. This created the 'pending dispute' that the agent then used at tool_call_32 to deny an otherwise-eligible $7,500 CLI.

root_cause: The agent did not see the conflict between the two requests. It did not act on the clean eligibility results by approving the CLI. Instead it filed the dispute first and then applied the no-pending-disputes rule to a dispute it had created itself.
key_facts_for_grader: Silver Rewards Card is mid-tier: 90-day account age, 90-day cooldown, <80% utilization, 3 on-time payments, max 50% increase
At the time of the checks, the account met every criterion: opened 11/15/2024, no prior CLI, no disputes, no pending replacement, $0 past due, 30% utilization, 3 on-time payments
Correct CLI outcome: approve, new_credit_limit 22500 ($7,500 increase), BEFORE filing the dispute
The agent's denial with 'pending_disputes' at tool_call_32 is wrong because the only dispute was the one the agent filed at tool_call_30, tool_call_31
The dispute filing was correct: goods_services_not_received, keep_active, last4 2791, purchase 10/10/2025, noticed 10/31/2025, full_refund, eligible_for_provisional_credit=true
acceptable_variations: A judge may name tool_call_32 (the denial) as the first critical error instead of tool_call_30, tool_call_31; both describe the same failure
A judge may or may not flag the transfer at tool_call_39
Repeated grants of get_card_last_4_digits are harmless
adjudicator_notes: The benchmark gold expects an approval to 22500 before the dispute, which agrees with policy. The first time the customer ran the user tool, he omitted credit_card_account_id; the agent re-granted it and he succeeded with 2791. The agent's statement that a denial does not trigger a cooldown is correct per doc_005.

summary: Sofia Papadopoulos wanted three things on her Gold Rewards Card: a fraud dispute for the CloudSync Storage $487.50 charge, a replacement card, and a CLI for a renovation. The agent had already read the CLI workflow (no pending disputes or replacement orders allowed). It still filed the dispute and ordered the replacement first [tool_call_28, tool_call_29], without telling her about the conflict. It then correctly capped her $4,000 request at $2,500 (50%) and submitted it. Finally it denied the CLI with 'pending_disputes', although she was otherwise fully eligible. The CLI should have been approved to $7,500 before the dispute and replacement were processed.

customer_requests.request: Credit limit increase ($4,000 initially, $5,000 to $9,000)
customer_requests.correct_handling: Gold is premium-tier, so the max increase is 50% = $2,500. Before submitting, tell her that $4,000 exceeds this and get her agreement to $2,500. Also tell her that a pending dispute or replacement order blocks a CLI, and process the CLI FIRST. Submit with submit_credit_limit_increase_request_7392(requested_increase_amount=2500), then run the eligibility checks. The account opened 03/20/2023, there is no prior CLI, no disputes and no replacements yet, past due is $0, utilization is about 9.75% ($487.50/$5,000), and she has 3 on-time payments. Approve with approve_credit_limit_increase_5847(new_credit_limit=7500).
customer_requests.agent_handling: Correctly said $4,000 exceeds the Gold max and got her agreement to $2,500 before submitting [assistant_msg_4], user_msg_4. But it submitted only after already filing the dispute and ordering the replacement [tool_call_31]. The checks then showed a pending dispute and a pending replacement [tool_result_36], tool_result_37, and it denied with 'pending_disputes' [tool_call_39]. At [assistant_msg_6] it refused to reorder.

customer_requests.request: Dispute fraudulent CloudSync Storage $487.50 charge
customer_requests.correct_handling: After the CLI decision, file file_credit_card_transaction_dispute_4829 with: txn_584f9c5d00_001, card_action cancel_and_reissue (replacement wanted), last4 7823, contacted_merchant false, purchase_date 11/11/2025, issue_noticed_date 11/12/2025, unauthorized_fraudulent_charge, full_refund. eligible_for_provisional_credit is true: fraud reason, $487.50 under the $10,000 premium cap, account 60+ days old, no prior disputes.
customer_requests.agent_handling: Filed the dispute with all the correct arguments [tool_call_28, tool_call_29]. The only problem was timing: it came before the CLI decision.

customer_requests.request: Replacement card due to compromised card
customer_requests.correct_handling: After the CLI decision, call order_replacement_credit_card_7291 with: cc_584f9c5d00_gold, shipping address 1456 Astoria Boulevard, Queens, NY 11102, reason fraud_suspected, expedited_shipping true (free on Gold and recommended for fraud).
customer_requests.agent_handling: Ordered it with the correct arguments [tool_call_28, tool_call_29] after confirming the address and expedited shipping. Again, this came before the CLI decision.

errors.finding: The agent filed the fraud dispute and ordered the replacement card before handling the CLI she had requested at user_msg_1. It had already read doc_007 at tool_result_18, which says a CLI requires no pending disputes and no pending replacement orders. It never told her about the conflict, so she had no chance to sequence the CLI first, and an otherwise-eligible $2,500 CLI was blocked.

The agent denied the CLI (denial_reason 'pending_disputes') because of the dispute and replacement it had itself just created. The correct outcome was approve_credit_limit_increase_5847 with new_credit_limit=7500.

first_critical_error.description: Filed the dispute and ordered the replacement before processing the requested CLI, and never warned her that both block CLI eligibility. This led directly to the CLI denial at tool_call_39.

root_cause: The agent followed her stated priority (fraud first) without connecting it to the CLI eligibility rules it had already read. So it created the blocking conditions itself, and then applied those rules mechanically to deny the CLI.
key_facts_for_grader: Gold Rewards Card is premium-tier: max CLI increase 50% of $5,000 = $2,500; 60-day account age/cooldown; <90% utilization; 3 on-time payments
The agent correctly refused the $4,000 request and had her agree to $2,500 BEFORE submitting
A pending dispute or pending replacement order blocks a CLI, so the CLI had to be approved (new limit $7,500) BEFORE the dispute and replacement
Before tool_call_28, tool_call_29 she met every CLI criterion; the denial at tool_call_39 was caused by the agent's own ordering

The dispute arguments (unauthorized_fraudulent_charge, cancel_and_reissue, last4 7823, contacted_merchant false, 11/11 and 11/12/2025, full_refund, provisional credit true) and the replacement arguments (fraud_suspected, expedited, address on file) were correct
acceptable_variations: A judge may name tool_call_39 (the denial) or assistant_msg_4/tool_call_31 as the first critical error, as long as it identifies the wrong ordering and the wrong denial
A judge may note that she asked to handle the fraud first; that does not excuse failing to tell her about the conflict
adjudicator_notes: The benchmark gold agrees: submit $2,500, approve to $7,500, then replacement and dispute. The dispute and replacement calls match the gold exactly; the missing approve call and the extra deny call are the DB mismatch.

summary: A landscaping-business owner with a Navy Blue business checking account ($3,200) wanted ONE better business checking account, then a business savings account funded from Navy Blue. The agent recommended and opened Lime Green Business Checking without asking about any of the customer's needs. Lime Green has a $5,000 minimum balance and a $25 fee waived only at $15,000, and the agent itself said at [assistant_msg_2] that Cobalt Blue fits better below $5,000. The savings part was handled correctly: Silver Plus Saver was opened [tool_call_24] and $3,200 was transferred from Navy Blue [tool_call_26]. The wrong checking account was opened.

customer_requests.request: Recommend ONE better business checking account for the landscaping business (needs: zero overdraft fees; under $50/month; ATM rebates of at least $15/month; fee waiver at a $3-5k balance; debit cash back on supplies) and open it
customer_requests.correct_handling: Ask about the business's needs, then recommend and open Cobalt Blue: $0 overdraft fee, $20 fee waived at a $2,500 daily balance, up to $15/month out-of-network ATM rebates, 1% debit cash back, up to 6 team debit cards. Call open_bank_account_4821(user_id=b5e8f2a1c9, account_type=business_checking, account_class='Cobalt Blue') after verification and the eligibility check (OPEN Green personal checking with $6,500 >= $500, no CLOSED accounts). Lime Green does not fit a $3-5k balance: $5,000 minimum balance, $25 fee waived only at $15,000, and no debit cash back.
customer_requests.agent_handling: At [assistant_msg_2] the agent recommended Lime Green before asking about the customer's needs, conditioned on keeping at least $5,000, and said Cobalt Blue was better below $5,000. When asked for one answer at [user_msg_2] (zero overdraft was the only stated need), it picked Lime Green at [assistant_msg_3] without asking about balance, fees, ATM or debit use. It saw at [tool_result_14] that the business checking held only $3,200, then opened 'Lime Green Business Checking' at [tool_call_15].

customer_requests.request: Recommend ONE business savings account (same-day ACH, $5-10k start, 15-20 withdrawals/month, relationship bonus) and open it
customer_requests.correct_handling: Recommend Silver Plus Saver Account: same-day ACH, $5,000 minimum, 20 free withdrawals per month, 2.5% APY below $25,000, +0.025% relationship bonus for multiple products, $10 fee below the minimum. Check eligibility (OPEN business checking open at least 30 days with at least $2,500: Navy Blue, opened 08/01/2025, $3,200). Open with account_type business_savings and account_class 'Silver Plus Saver Account'.
customer_requests.agent_handling: At [assistant_msg_6] it first leaned toward Bronze. After the customer gave criteria at [user_msg_6], it recommended Silver Plus Saver at [assistant_msg_7] with correct facts (same-day ACH, $5,000 minimum, 20 withdrawals, 2.5% APY, 0.025% relationship bonus, $10 fee). It re-checked accounts at [tool_call_23] and opened the account at [tool_call_24].

customer_requests.request: Fund the new savings account by moving all $3,200 from Navy Blue business checking
customer_requests.correct_handling: Offer to transfer the opening deposit (doc 004 step 5). On authorization, call transfer_funds_between_bank_accounts_7291(source=biz_chk_b5e8f2a1c9, destination=new savings account c1b48f17bb35e876, amount=3200).
customer_requests.agent_handling: Offered the transfer at [assistant_msg_8], unlocked the tool at [tool_call_25] and transferred $3,200 from biz_chk_b5e8f2a1c9 to c1b48f17bb35e876 at [tool_call_26]. It correctly noted that $1,800 more is needed to reach the $5,000 minimum.

errors.finding: The agent recommended Lime Green without asking about the customer's needs, saying only that it assumed a $5,000+ balance. On its own this is a process weakness. It becomes critical when acted on at assistant_msg_3/tool_call_15.

The customer asked for the single best fit. The agent picked Lime Green without checking the balance condition it had itself said was decisive. Lime Green needs a $5,000 minimum balance, waives its $25 fee only at $15,000, and has no debit cash back. The customer's business funds were $3,200 (seen at tool_result_14). Cobalt Blue fits: $0 overdraft fee, $20 fee waived at $2,500, 1% debit cash back, up to $15/month ATM rebates.

Opened business_checking with account_class 'Lime Green Business Checking' instead of 'Cobalt Blue'. The agent had just seen at tool_result_14 that the customer's business checking balance was $3,200, below Lime Green's $5,000 minimum.

first_critical_error.description: Recommended Lime Green Business Checking as the single best fit ($5,000 minimum, fee waived only at $15,000, no debit cash back) without asking about the customer's balance or usage. Cobalt Blue was the correct account; Lime Green was opened at tool_call_15.

root_cause: The agent recommended a 'premium' account up front without asking about the customer's needs, then ignored its own $5,000 balance condition even after seeing the $3,200 business balance.
key_facts_for_grader: The correct business checking account was Cobalt Blue, not Lime Green
Lime Green: $25/month fee waived only at $15,000; $5,000 minimum balance; $0 overdraft fee; no debit cash back
Cobalt Blue: $0 overdraft fee, $20 fee waived at a $2,500 daily balance, 1% debit cash back, up to $15/month ATM rebates
The agent never asked about balance, ATM or debit needs before recommending; it saw a $3,200 business balance at tool_result_14 and still opened Lime Green at tool_call_15
Silver Plus Saver recommendation, opening and the $3,200 transfer from biz_chk_b5e8f2a1c9 were correct
acceptable_variations: A judge may put the first critical error at assistant_msg_2 (first recommendation) or tool_call_15 (the account-opening call) instead of assistant_msg_3
Leaning toward Bronze Saver first at assistant_msg_6 before correcting to Silver Plus is not a failure
Re-reading the accounts list at tool_call_23 before opening savings is fine
adjudicator_notes: Lime Green does have a $0 overdraft fee, so the agent's claim at assistant_msg_3 is factually true. The failure is the unexamined fit: the simulator never revealed its other criteria because the agent never asked, which is the agent's fault, not the simulator's. Business checking eligibility (OPEN Green personal checking $6,500, no closed accounts) and savings eligibility (Navy Blue opened 08/01/2025, $3,200 >= $2,500) were met. summary: Ahmad Razali asked for a review of the November ATM fees on his Purple, Light Blue, Dark Green and Evergreen checking accounts. The agent verified him, pulled all four histories and applied fee_refund credits at [tool_call_22 through tool_call_25]: Purple $27.00, Light Blue $17.00, Dark Green $7.50 and Evergreen $6.50. These are gross overcharge refunds. Policy requires a NET correction that also subtracts undercharged and missing fees. The correct amounts are Light Blue $14.50, Dark Green $4.75 and Evergreen $3.70, so three of the four credits are over-credited.

customer_requests.request: Review November ATM fees on all four checking accounts and correct any errors
customer_requests.correct_handling: Verify the customer and log it. Pull the accounts and the transactions for chk_ar72c5d8e3_1..4. Compare each ATM fee to the account's fee schedule. Apply ONE apply_checking_account_credit_5829 per account with credit_type fee_refund for the NET correction: overcharges minus undercharged or missing fees. Purple $27.00: 11/03 Rho-Bank fee $2.50; foreign fees 11/07 London $8.00 and 11/09 Kuala Lumpur $10.50 (Purple foreign fee is $0); 11/11 $3.50 fee/rebate correction $3.50; duplicate 11/15 $2.50. Light Blue $14.50: 11/03 Rho-Bank $2.50 (+2.50); 11/05 and 11/06 domestic out-of-network fees should be free as the first 2 (+5.00); 11/08 and 11/09 foreign fees should be free as the first 2 (+8.00); 11/13 foreign fee $5.50 should be $4.00 (+1.50); 11/10 PNC $150 is the 3rd domestic out-of-network withdrawal and is missing its $2.50 fee (-2.50). Dark Green $4.75: 11/02 Rho-Bank $1.50 (+1.50); 11/07 $200 fee $4.00 should be 1% = $2.00 (+2.00); 11/12 $400 foreign fee $10.00 should hit the $6.00 cap (+4.00); 11/05 $50 fee $0.50 should be the $1.50 minimum (-1.00); 11/13 TD $175 is missing its $1.75 fee (-1.75). Evergreen $3.70: 11/03 Rho-Bank $1.50 (+1.50); 11/08 $400 fee $4.00 should hit the $2.50 max (+1.50); 11/11 $350 foreign fee $10.50 should be 2% = $7.00 (+3.50); 11/09 $100 foreign fee $2.00 should be the $3.00 minimum (-1.00); 11/12 TD $180 is missing its $1.80 fee (-1.80).
customer_requests.agent_handling: Verified the customer with DOB and phone and logged it at [tool_call_5]. It retrieved the accounts and all four transaction histories at [tool_call_15]-[tool_result_20]. Then, without first presenting findings, it applied credits at [tool_call_22 through tool_call_25] of $27.00 to Purple, $17.00 to Light Blue, $7.50 to Dark Green and $6.50 to Evergreen. These counted only overcharges. It did not net out the missing Light Blue 11/10 $2.50 fee, the Dark Green 11/05 $1.00 minimum shortfall and missing 11/13 $1.75 fee, or the Evergreen 11/09 $1.00 minimum shortfall and missing 11/12 $1.80 fee. It reported a $58.00 total at [assistant_msg_3]-[assistant_msg_5].

errors.finding: Light Blue (chk_ar72c5d8e3_2) was credited $17.00 instead of the net $14.50. The 11/10 PNC $150 withdrawal was the 3rd domestic out-of-network withdrawal after the 2 free ones, and its $2.50 fee was never charged. Policy doc _017 requires the credit to reflect the net correction across all fee discrepancies.

Dark Green (chk_ar72c5d8e3_3) was credited $7.50 instead of the net $4.75. Two undercharges were ignored. The 11/05 $50 withdrawal was charged $0.50 when the 1% fee has a $1.50 minimum (-$1.00). The 11/13 TD Bank $175 withdrawal had no fee when it should have been $1.75 (-$1.75).

Evergreen (chk_ar72c5d8e3_4) was credited $6.50 instead of the net $3.70. Two undercharges were ignored. The 11/09 $100 foreign withdrawal was charged $2.00 when the 2% fee has a $3.00 minimum (-$1.00). The 11/12 TD Bank $180 withdrawal had no 1% fee when it should have been $1.80 (-$1.80).

The agent applied all four credits before presenting its findings or confirming with the customer. The customer had only asked for a review. This is not critical because the customer clearly wanted the fees corrected.

first_critical_error.description: Applied gross overcharge refunds instead of net corrections: Light Blue $17.00 (should be $14.50), Dark Green $7.50 (should be $4.75), Evergreen $6.50 (should be $3.70). The 1-credit-per-account rule makes these unrecoverable in the session.

Correct credits: Purple $27.00, Light Blue $14.50, Dark Green $4.75, Evergreen $3.70 (all fee_refund)

summary: Carlos Rodriguez's wallet was stolen with debit cards for his Evergreen (Premium), Light Blue (Entry) and Green (Mid) accounts. It ordered the Evergreen replacement (RUSH $35, PREMIUM $0) and the Green replacement (STANDARD, CLASSIC), and correctly deferred Light Blue because of the replacement limit ($25 fee) and the 48-hour wait. However, it never checked transaction history. It therefore closed the Green card without finding the pending $89.99 Amazon refund and without getting the customer's written acknowledgment, which policy requires before closing a card with a pending refund.

Tell the customer to either wait for it to process (3-5 business days) or acknowledge in writing that the refund will be credited to the Green checking account. Close dbc_cr89a2b3c4_green only after that acknowledgment.

Tried to close the frozen cards (errored, tool_call_27, tool_call_28, tool_call_29), unfroze them (tool_call_31, tool_call_32, tool_call_33), and closed all three as stolen (tool_call_34, tool_call_35, tool_call_36), including Green, without disclosing the pending refund or getting acknowledgment.

errors.finding: Closed the Green card dbc_cr89a2b3c4_green without checking for pending refunds. Policy requirement 5 for card closure says a card with a pending refund cannot be closed unless the customer waits for the refund to process or acknowledges in writing that it will be credited to the linked checking account. The Green account had a pending +$89.99 AMAZON.COM RETURN refund, which the agent never retrieved, disclosed or got acknowledgment for. The agent had read this requirement (tool_result_22-tool_result_25) but never called get_bank_account_transactions_9173.
Tried to close the cards while they were FROZEN; the calls errored harmlessly before the agent unfroze them.

root_cause: The agent read the pending-transaction and pending-refund requirements but never retrieved transaction history, so it could not see the $89.99 pending refund on the Green account and closed that card without the required acknowledgment.
key_facts_for_grader: The Green account (chk_cr89a2b3c4_3) had a pending +$89.99 'REFUND - AMAZON.COM RETURN'; closure required the customer to wait or acknowledge in writing that the refund goes to the checking account

Green replacement STANDARD/0, CLASSIC/0 had the correct arguments

The remaining work (credit card replacements via order_replacement_credit_card_7291, closing and replacing debit cards, fraud disputes) was within its capabilities. The stolen credit cards were left active: no replacement orders were placed for the Gold Rewards Card (3829) or EcoCard (5147). The stolen debit cards were left frozen but not closed or replaced. The fraud disputes (CryptoMiner Pro $299.99, FastCrypto Exchange $199.99, SuperGaming Online $149.95) were never filed.

summary: Marcus Chen asked to dispute four debit card transactions. On the lost Blue card (4827): ElectroniX Outlet $347.50 (11/07, card-present fraud) and FitLife Premium $89.99 (11/10, recurring charge after cancellation). On the Green Fee-Free card (7391), which he still has: a Rho-Bank ATM #2847 shortfall of $100 on 11/09 and CryptoGems Store $523.17 (11/12, online fraud). The agent verified him, chose the right categories, amounts, transaction types and card_action values, closed both cards, and ordered a standard Classic Blue replacement while deferring Green Fee-Free under the 48-hour rule. But it never asked when each issue was noticed. It filed every dispute with discovery_date 11/14/2025, even though the customer said he called FitLife about the charge on 11/11 and the ATM shortfall was obvious on 11/09. It also applied the lost Blue card's compromised PIN ('yes_observed') to the two disputes on the Green card, which was never lost.

customer_requests.request: Speak to a human agent (asked once at the start)

Provisional credit is not required for this category but may be given at discretion, so either true (gold) or false is defensible.
customer_requests.agent_handling: Filed with the correct category and fields but discovery_date 11/14/2025, with provisional false, at [tool_call_26 through tool_call_29].

customer_requests.correct_handling: Arguments: btxn_3bd1ba6ad800, atm_cash_discrepancy, disputed_amount 100, atm_withdrawal, card in possession, pin_compromised 'no' (this card was never lost), keep_active, provisional credit true. discovery_date should be 11/09/2025, because the shortfall was evident at the machine; the agent should have asked.

customer_requests.correct_handling: Both cards' fraud disputes map to close_and_reissue, and the agent must then perform the most severe action itself. Close the Blue card (reason lost) and order a replacement: STANDARD $0, CLASSIC $0, 1847 Pine Street, Seattle, WA 98101. Close the Green Fee-Free card (fraud) and defer its replacement 48 hours (entry tier, standard only).
customer_requests.agent_handling: Closed the Blue card (lost) and the Green card (fraud_suspected) at [tool_call_31, tool_call_32] with the customer's consent ([user_msg_5]). Ordered the Blue replacement STANDARD/$0/CLASSIC/$0 at [tool_call_34]. Told the customer the Green replacement can be ordered on or after 11/16/2025.

errors.finding: The FitLife Premium $89.99 dispute (btxn_d1f51e0a0db9) was filed with discovery_date 11/14/2025. At [user_msg_4] the customer said he called FitLife about this charge on 11/11, so the issue was noticed by 11/11/2025. The agent never asked for discovery dates.

The ATM #2847 cash discrepancy dispute (btxn_3bd1ba6ad800, $100) was filed with discovery_date 11/14/2025. The shortfall (requested $200, received $100) was necessarily noticed at the machine on 11/09/2025. The agent should have asked rather than defaulting to today.

pin_compromised='yes_observed' was recorded on both Green Fee-Free card disputes: ATM btxn_3bd1ba6ad800 and CryptoGems btxn_d74e8a798f95. The customer's PIN compromise (a sticky note in the lost wallet) concerned the lost Blue card. The Green card was never lost, and the CryptoGems charge was card-not-present, so these should be 'no' (or the agent should have asked per card). (Severity debatable: the customer's 'my PIN was compromised' answer at user_msg_3 did not name a card.)

On the ElectroniX dispute, the PIN was kept on a sticky note in the lost wallet. Gold records 'yes_shared' with provisional_credit_eligible false. The agent recorded 'yes_observed' with provisional true. The KB definitions ('shared with someone' vs 'observed/skimmed') do not fit this case cleanly, so this is ambiguous rather than clearly wrong.

first_critical_error.description: The disputes were filed with discovery_date 11/14/2025 for FitLife (customer called the merchant on 11/11) and the ATM shortfall (noticed on 11/09), and with pin_compromised 'yes_observed' on the Green card disputes even though that card and its PIN were never lost.

root_cause: The agent asked one global set of questions (possession, PIN, merchant contact) and never asked a per-transaction discovery date. It then applied the lost card's answers and 'today' to every dispute instead of mapping the facts to each transaction.
key_facts_for_grader: FitLife $89.99 discovery date should be 11/11/2025 (customer called the merchant that day), not 11/14/2025
The agent never asked the discovery date for the ATM #2847 $100 shortfall; it was evident at the machine on 11/09/2025, so recording 11/14/2025 is likely wrong
Only the Blue card (4827) was lost with the PIN; the Green Fee-Free card (7391) disputes should have pin_compromised 'no', not 'yes_observed'

Categories were correct: card_present_fraud, recurring_charge_after_cancellation, atm_cash_discrepancy ($100), card_not_present_fraud. card_action values were correct: close_and_reissue, keep_active, keep_active, close_and_reissue

Closing both cards and ordering only the Blue replacement (STANDARD, CLASSIC, $0) is correct per policy, with the Green Fee-Free replacement deferred 48 hours. The benchmark gold omitting the closures is a gold defect
Police report recommended for the $523.17 CryptoGems fraud: correct
acceptable_variations: provisional_credit_eligible for FitLife (recurring_charge_after_cancellation) may be true or false: the KB says it is 'not required (but may be offered at discretion)'
ElectroniX pin_compromised 'yes_shared' vs 'yes_observed', and the resulting provisional credit decision, are ambiguous; a judge need not flag them
customer_max_liability_amount 50 on all disputes is consistent with gold
A judge may group the date and PIN errors as one 'did not gather per-dispute details' failure
A judge may treat the Green Fee-Free pin_compromised value as ambiguous; the FitLife discovery date (11/11 stated at user_msg_4, filed as 11/14) is the clearest critical error
adjudicator_notes: The benchmark gold is flawed here. It never closes the Blue card before ordering a replacement, and never performs close_and_reissue on the Green Fee-Free card, even though doc_031 requires the agent to perform the most severe card action itself. So the agent's two closures are correct, not unexpected writes. The CryptoGems discovery date 11/14/2025 is correct: the confusing 'January 9th' script line was never spoken. The fail rests on the FitLife and ATM discovery dates and the PIN field on the Green card, all of which conflict with what the customer said. The DB reward of 0 partly reflects gold defects, but the verdict agrees with it.

override_reason: The action-based reward is 0 because of two argument mismatches and two 'extra' calls, all of which are policy-supported. (1) On the Austin Coffee Roasters duplicate charge, the agent set pin_compromised 'yes_shared' and provisional_credit_eligible false. The card's PIN really was shared, and the customer had not contacted the merchant, which the KB lists as a 'not required' condition for non-fraud disputes. (2) The GameStop dispute was for $425, the unauthorized excess over the exactly $50 the customer authorized and confirmed, rather than $475. (3) The extra freeze_debit_card_3892 is required by doc_031: the agent must perform the most severe card_action, freeze_pending_investigation, for the Green card. (4) The extra reset_debit_card_pin_6284 was explicitly requested by the customer.
summary: Diana Kowalski disputed four debit card transactions. On the Blue card (5291): a third-party QuickCash ATM shortfall (requested $250, got $100) and Premium Photo Frames $189.50 not received. It correctly told her no affidavit was needed (the ATM claim is $150, not over $200) and that third-party ATM claims take up to 90 days. At her request it reset the Green card PIN and froze the card pending investigation.

customer_requests.agent_handling: Filed with the correct transaction, category, type, date and keep_active, with pin_compromised 'yes_shared' (accurate for this card) and provisional credit false, at [tool_call_34]. It told the customer why and recommended contacting the merchant.

customer_requests.correct_handling: Arguments: btxn_333f5b136543, unauthorized_transaction (family member, fraud not suspected), discovery 11/12/2025, pin_compromised 'yes_shared', provisional credit false, card_action freeze_pending_investigation, then actually freeze the card. disputed_amount: gold uses $475. Disputing only the $425 excess over the confirmed $50 authorization is also reasonable.

customer_requests.correct_handling: Explain the options. Close-and-reissue on an entry-tier account means a 48-hour wait and standard shipping. Otherwise reset the PIN and freeze the card, since freeze_pending_investigation is the most severe card_action across the card's disputes and must be performed.

The stronger KB basis for 'not required' is that the customer had not contacted the merchant (a non-fraud dispute). The outcome is still policy-consistent.

The GameStop $425 vs $475 is a judgement call: the KB just says 'the dollar amount being disputed', and the customer explicitly confirmed she authorized exactly $50.

summary: Valeria Montes wanted to dispute four debit card transactions. On the Evergreen card (3847): a Bella's Bistro $47.50 duplicate and a Whole Foods $100 overcharge. On the Light Blue card (6129): an EveryonePay $275 transfer and a TechWorld Electronics $412.88 fraud from 10/05. The agent verified her and found the existing open dispute on the entry-tier Light Blue account (limit 2). She chose TechWorld, and the agent filed three disputes with correct categories, closed the Light Blue card and correctly deferred its replacement. But for the late-reported TechWorld fraud, a transaction 40 days old that the customer acknowledged she was reporting late, it set customer_max_liability_amount to $50 and told her 'Your maximum potential liability is $50'. Per KB this is the $500 tier, so liability is min($500, $412.88) = $412.88.

Because the transaction is from 10/05 and is being reported 40 days later (past 2 business days from the statement but within 60 days), the $500 tier applies: customer_max_liability_amount = min($500, $412.88) = $412.88, and the customer should be told so. Do not file EveryonePay now.
customer_requests.agent_handling: Correctly found the open dispute and the remaining slot ([tool_result_11], [assistant_msg_3]), and filed only TechWorld with the correct category, type, pin, provisional and card_action ([tool_call_24, tool_call_25, tool_call_26]). errors.finding: The TechWorld Electronics $412.88 dispute (transaction 10/05/2025, reported 11/14/2025) was filed with customer_max_liability_amount 50. Under the Reg E tiers in doc_031 (measured from the statement), it was reported more than 2 business days after the statement but within 60 days, so the cap is $500. That makes liability min($500, $412.88) = $412.88. The customer herself acknowledged reporting late.

The agent told the customer 'Your maximum potential liability is $50 based on the reporting time' for the late-reported TechWorld fraud. Her exposure is actually up to $412.88 (the $500 tier, capped at the disputed amount).

Whole Foods customer_max_liability_amount was set to 100 (gold 50). The agent measured the reporting window from discovery rather than from the statement. For non-fraud error disputes this field has little practical effect.

first_critical_error.description: The TechWorld $412.88 dispute (10/05 transaction, reported 11/14) was filed with customer_max_liability_amount $50 instead of the $500-tier value of $412.88.

root_cause: The agent measured the Reg E liability window from the customer's discovery date (today) instead of from the statement showing the transaction. So it treated a 40-day-old fraud as reported within 2 business days.
key_facts_for_grader: TechWorld $412.88 (10/05/2025) was reported 11/14/2025, more than 2 business days after the statement but within 60 days, so the $500 tier applies and customer_max_liability_amount should be $412.88 (min of $500 and the disputed amount), not $50
The agent told the customer her liability was capped at $50 ([assistant_msg_4]), which is wrong
The dispute-limit handling was correct: Light Blue (entry tier, max 2 open) already had one open dispute, so only TechWorld was filed and EveryonePay was deferred
Light Blue card closed as fraud_suspected and replacement correctly NOT ordered (entry-tier 48-hour wait)
Bella's Bistro duplicate, $47.50: first transaction, keep_active. Whole Foods incorrect_amount, $100, signature_purchase, contacted merchant, no provisional credit: correct
acceptable_variations: Bella's Bistro provisional credit false is defensible: the KB 'not required' condition covers non-fraud disputes where the merchant was not contacted. Gold has true
A TechWorld liability of $500 (newer gold) instead of $412.88 is acceptable; the key point is that $50 is wrong
Duplicate liability 47.5 vs 50 and Whole Foods 100 vs 50 are minor or acceptable
Not recommending a police report for TechWorld ($412.88 is under $500) is correct
adjudicator_notes: The KB wording mixes reference points: doc_031 says 'based on when they noticed' but its tiers say 'within 2 business days of statement'. Because the transaction is 40 days old and the customer explicitly said she was reporting late, the statement-based $500 tier is the policy-consistent reading, and gold agrees ($412.88; a newer gold version has $500). The other gold mismatches (duplicate provisional credit, liability values on non-fraud disputes) are defensible and not counted as critical. The DB reward of 0 is consistent with the verdict.

summary: Jordan Williams asked to file four debit-card disputes, one at a time: a Rho-Bank ATM #4827 shortfall of $100 (Blue), a duplicate $89.99 CityFit Gym charge on 11/06 (Blue), a claimed $200 shortfall at Rho-Bank ATM #5921 (Green Fee-Free), and a Prime Streaming charge he remembered as $49.99 (Green Fee-Free).
