first_critical_error.description: The duplicate-charge dispute was filed on the later CityFit charge btxn_c3d4e5f6g703 instead of the earliest one, btxn_b2c3d4e5f602, as doc_031 requires. (The identical first attempt at tool_call_25 errored on transaction_type, so tool_call_26 is the call that took effect.)

root_cause: The agent knew the earliest-duplicate rule but misread the reverse-chronological transaction list. It took the first-listed of the two same-date CityFit charges, which is the most recent, as the earlier one.
key_facts_for_grader: The duplicate CityFit Gym dispute must be on btxn_b2c3d4e5f602 (the earlier of the two 11/06/2025 $89.99 charges); the agent filed on btxn_c3d4e5f6g703
Transactions are returned in reverse chronological order, so the first-listed same-date duplicate (btxn_c3d4e5f6g703) is the later one
The ATM #4827 $100 dispute (btxn_a1b2c3d4e501) and the Prime Streaming $14.99 dispute (btxn_f6g7h8i9j006, provisional credit false) were filed correctly
The agent correctly caught that ATM #5921 shows a $200 debit (not $500) and that Prime Streaming was $14.99 (not $49.99), and did not file the ATM #5921 dispute after the customer chose to skip it
acceptable_variations: customer_max_liability_amount 0 vs 50 may be flagged as minor or not at all; it is not the basis of the fail
Flagging the affidavit statement for a $200 claim as minor misinformation is fine, as is not flagging it
The judge may point to tool_call_25 or tool_call_26 as the first critical error, since both used the wrong transaction ID
Not explicitly offering a formal dispute on ATM #5921 despite the journal mismatch is acceptable, since the customer chose to skip
adjudicator_notes: The verdict agrees with DB reward 0. The alignment shows a wrong transaction_id on 085_7 (gold btxn_b2c3d4e5f602) and liability 0 vs 50 on all disputes. I base the fail only on the duplicate transaction ID: doc_031 explicitly says to dispute the earliest duplicate, and the tool output is reverse chronological. Confidence is medium because both duplicates share the same date, so 'earliest' has to be inferred from list order and ID sequence. The liability difference is treated as minor because the KB's liability tiers address unauthorized activity.

The agent had the tool and enough information (card in possession, suspected skimming, so card_present_fraud/pin_purchase, PIN unknown, $500 liability tier, provisional credit eligible, close_and_reissue), and it already had dispute capacity (3 of 4 on Evergreen). Not knowing the channel for certain is not a reason to transfer when the customer described suspected skimming.

root_cause: The agent retrieved the ATM deposit record but filed in parallel without comparing it to the customer's claim. It then could not amend the filed dispute, and it also treated the TechWorld channel and discovery-date uncertainty as reasons to hand off instead of filing.
key_facts_for_grader: The ATM #6172 deposit record shows $400 credited, so the atm_deposit_not_credited dispute should be $100; the agent filed $200 at tool_call_30, tool_call_31 after seeing $400 at tool_result_29
The TechWorld $625 card_present_fraud dispute was never filed; the agent transferred to a human instead
The Green Fee-Free account is Entry tier with a max of 2 open disputes; the agent correctly refused the third (CryptoMiner) dispute
The Evergreen account (Premium tier, max 4) had 1 existing open dispute, so 3 more could be filed
QuickCash $100 third-party ATM, SupplyPro $189.99 goods-not-received, and Phoenix Kitchen Supply $200 incorrect-amount disputes were filed correctly
Card 9251 closure and the free EXPEDITED + PREMIUM replacement to 1520 East McDowell Road were correct
acceptable_variations: customer_max_liability_amount 0 on the non-fraud disputes (gold 50) need not be flagged as critical
A judge may view the TechWorld transfer as partly driven by the customer's confusing '01/12/2026' discovery date; the fail stands on the ATM deposit amount alone
Flagging the unnecessary affidavit instruction for a $100 claim is optional (minor)
pin_purchase vs signature_purchase for TechWorld is a judgement call; card_present_fraud is the key
adjudicator_notes: The simulator stated an impossible discovery date ('01/12', then '01/12/2026') for TechWorld while the current date was 11/14/2025. This is the known task_086 script issue, and it partly drove the agent's late-reporting reasoning and the TechWorld transfer. It does not affect the ATM deposit error, which the agent committed on its own with the contradicting record in hand, so I do not exclude. The extra transfer_to_human_agents is not in the gold. The QuickCash affidavit remark is minor. The leaked '</think>' text in assistant_msg_3 is cosmetic.

adjudicator_notes: Consistent with the prior gold for task_012: gpt-5.6-sol t1 (fail: no transfer offered, redirected to support) and kimi-k3 t2 (pass: admitted gap and transferred). Recommended Hunter Green as the only fit [assistant_msg_3], wrongly dismissing others with 'the higher-APY options require $15k-$25k+ balances' (Sky Blue at 1.25% APY has no funding/minimum requirement; Lime Green's minimum is $5,000). Verified correctly [tool_call_21, tool_call_23], checked eligibility [tool_call_25], and opened Hunter Green [tool_call_29].

errors.finding: Recommended Hunter Green and claimed it was the only account meeting all requirements. Sky Blue (1.25% APY, $15/mo ATM rebates, $0 overdraft, no funding requirement) and Lime Green (1.5% APY, $25/mo rebates, $0 overdraft, $5,000 minimum) also qualify, and the active November 2025 promotion (11/01-11/30/2025) requires Sky Blue first, then Lime Green; other qualifying accounts may be recommended only if neither fits. The agent also misstated that the higher-APY options require $15k-$25k+ balances.
Opened business checking with account_class 'Hunter Green' instead of 'Sky Blue'.

first_critical_error.description: Recommended Hunter Green as the single best account, ignoring the active November 2025 promotion that prioritizes Sky Blue (then Lime Green) when multiple accounts qualify.

root_cause: The agent compared product features but never retrieved the business checking promotion policies, so it did not apply the active November priority order (Sky Blue, then Lime Green).
key_facts_for_grader: Sky Blue, Lime Green and Hunter Green all meet the four stated requirements (ATM rebates >= $15, $0 overdraft, balance requirement < $10k, APY >= 1%)
Active promotion doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_013 (11/01-11/30/2025) ranks Sky Blue first, Lime Green second; current date 11/14/2025; the October promotion (doc_014) ended 11/12/2025
Agent recommended Hunter Green at assistant_msg_3 and opened account_class 'Hunter Green' at tool_call_29; correct was 'Sky Blue'
Agent never opened doc_013 or doc_014 (only saw their filenames in tool_result_16)
Verification (DOB + email, logged at tool_call_23) and eligibility (Green checking OPEN, $2,850, no closed accounts) were handled correctly
acceptable_variations: Citing tool_call_29 (the account opening) as the first critical error instead of assistant_msg_3

Arguing Lime Green rather than Sky Blue is the correct pick because the customer called the business 'established (not brand new)' and Sky Blue requires formation within 4 years — still a fail for Hunter Green either way, since Lime Green outranks Hunter Green under the active promotion
Flagging the misstatement about higher-APY accounts requiring $15k-$25k+ balances as a separate misinformation error
adjudicator_notes: Consistent with prior gold gpt-5.6-sol__task_070__t0 (Hunter Green = fail) and kimi-k3__task_070__t3 (Sky Blue = pass). Nuance: the simulator added two unscripted statements in user_msg_2 — that the business is 'established (not brand new)' and a preference for no/easy-to-waive monthly fee. Neither is a firm requirement (age vs. Sky Blue's 4-year limit was never established; the fee item is phrased as a preference), and even discounting Sky Blue the active promotion puts Lime Green ahead of Hunter Green. Not excluded: the agent never looked at the promotion policy at all. Confidence medium only because of these unscripted remarks.

summary: Kim Junho asked for a review of November ATM fees on his Blue, Green and Light Green checking accounts. The agent verified him, pulled all three histories, and correctly credited Blue $9.50 [tool_call_25] and Green $9.00 [tool_call_26], but credited Light Green $4.50 [tool_call_27] when the net correction is $1.50. In [assistant_msg_10] and [assistant_msg_11] it admitted the net owed was $1.50 and told the customer the $3.00 excess would simply remain on the account.

customer_requests.request: Review November ATM fees on Blue, Green and Light Green checking accounts and correct any errors
customer_requests.correct_handling: Verify (2 of DOB/email/phone/address) and log_verification, retrieve all three histories, then make ONE net apply_checking_account_credit_5829 call per account (doc_017: exact net amount, one call per account, 14-day cooldown). Blue chk_kj93a7b2e1_1 (out-of-network 1% capped at $3.00, Rho-Bank ATMs free, foreign 3% min $5): 11/05 $300 Wells Fargo fee $4.50 vs $3.00 (+$1.50), 11/09 $500 Shinhan Seoul foreign fee $20.00 vs $15.00 (+$5.00), 11/13 Rho-Bank ATM charged $3.00 vs $0 (+$3.00) = $9.50 fee_refund. Green chk_kj93a7b2e1_2 ($3.00 flat out-of-network, in-network free, foreign 3% min $5): 11/07 Rho-Bank ATM $3.00 vs $0 (+$3.00), 11/09 $400 Woori Seoul foreign fee $15.00 vs $12.00 (+$3.00), duplicate $3.00 fee on 11/15 PNC (+$3.00) = $9.00 fee_refund. Light Green chk_kj93a7b2e1_3 (4 free domestic out-of-network withdrawals then $1.50; foreign $2.00 up to $100 / $3.50 to $300 / $5.00 above): 11/03 BofA $60 (2nd withdrawal) charged $1.50 vs free (+$1.50), 11/15 $150 KB Kookmin Jeju charged Tier-3 $5.00 vs Tier-2 $3.50 (+$1.50), 11/17 TD Bank $65 (7th withdrawal) missing its $1.50 fee (-$1.50) = net $1.50 fee_refund.
customer_requests.agent_handling: Verified and logged [tool_call_3, tool_call_5], retrieved accounts and all three histories [tool_call_17, tool_call_19, tool_call_20, tool_call_21]. Applied $9.50 to Blue [tool_call_25] and $9.00 to Green [tool_call_26] (both correct) and $4.50 to Light Green [tool_call_27] (should be $1.50). Its itemization identified all three Light Green discrepancies and the $1.50 net, but it acknowledged the $3.00 over-credit and left it in place [assistant_msg_10, assistant_msg_11].

errors.finding: Applied a $4.50 fee_refund to Light Green chk_kj93a7b2e1_3 instead of the $1.50 net correction (+$1.50 for the 11/03 fee on the 2nd, free withdrawal; +$1.50 for the 11/15 $150 foreign withdrawal charged Tier-3 $5.00 instead of Tier-2 $3.50; -$1.50 for the missing fee on the 11/17 7th withdrawal). doc_017 requires the credit to equal the exact net correction; over-credit of $3.00.

After recognizing the net owed was $1.50, the agent told the customer the extra $3.00 'remains on your account in your favor' rather than flagging it; the error itself is the tool call, and one-credit-per-account means it could not be re-done.

first_critical_error.description: Credited $4.50 to Light Green chk_kj93a7b2e1_3 instead of the correct net $1.50.

root_cause: The agent applied credits before finishing its own net calculation for Light Green; its later itemization reached the correct $1.50 net but the over-credit had already posted.
key_facts_for_grader: Correct net credits: Blue $9.50, Green $9.00, Light Green $1.50 (all fee_refund)
Blue $9.50 (tool_call_25) and Green $9.00 (tool_call_26) were correct
Light Green was credited $4.50 at tool_call_27; correct net is $1.50 (+1.50 on 11/03, +1.50 on 11/15 foreign tier, -1.50 missing 11/17 fee)
The agent itself acknowledged in assistant_msg_10/11 that the net owed was $1.50 and the $3.00 excess was left on the account
Verification and log_verification preceded account access
acceptable_variations: Categorizing the Light Green error as incorrect_arguments instead of calculation_error
A judge may credit the agent's transparency in assistant_msg_10, but it must still fail the trace because the posted credit amount is wrong
adjudicator_notes: Consistent with prior golds for task_073 (opus-5 t1 fail for wrong Green/Light Green amounts; qwen t3 pass with $9.50/$9.00/$1.50). Amounts re-derived from tool_result_21 and the Light Green fee schedule. Benchmark gold and policy agree.

summary: Marco Vitiello wanted to open the personal checking account with the lowest ATM fees for about 18 out-of-network, foreign-currency ATM withdrawals of about $350 over a 3-month trip. The agent recommended Purple Account at [assistant_msg_2]. At [assistant_msg_3] it told him both Purple and Green Fee-Free charge $0 in Rho fees for his withdrawals, although it had just read doc_checking_accounts_purple_account_012 ($2.50 per out-of-network withdrawal) at [tool_result_13]. It verified him and opened a Purple Account at [tool_call_26]. The correct account is Green Fee-Free ($0 out-of-network + $0 foreign).

customer_requests.request: Recommend and open the personal checking account with the lowest ATM fees for out-of-network foreign-currency ATM withdrawals (6/month x $350 for 3 months)
customer_requests.correct_handling: For an out-of-network foreign ATM, both the out-of-network fee and the foreign ATM fee apply. Green Fee-Free Account: $0 out-of-network + $0 foreign = $0 in Rho fees, $500 daily ATM limit (enough for $350), maintenance fee waived with a $150 minimum daily balance. Purple: $2.50 x 18 = $45 (its $30/month rebate covers ATM operator fees, not Rho's fee). Bluest: $2.00 x 18 = $36 but needs a $75,000 opening deposit. Light Blue about $78, Evergreen about $171, Blue/Green about $243. Gold Years, Light Green and Dark Green are age-restricted (he is 31). Recommend Green Fee-Free, verify (2 of DOB/email/phone/address) and log it, check eligibility (18+, at most 4 personal checking accounts, none closed for cause in 6 months), confirm, then call open_bank_account_4821 with user_id mv93f8a7b2, account_type checking, account_class 'Green Fee-Free Account'.
customer_requests.agent_handling: At [assistant_msg_2] the agent ranked Purple first as 'likely your best fit'. It listed Purple's $0 foreign ATM fee but left out its $2.50 out-of-network fee. When the customer gave his usage and asked 'are you sure' at [user_msg_2], the agent read doc_checking_accounts_purple_account_012 at [tool_call_13]. It still said at [assistant_msg_3] that both accounts charge $0 Rho fees for his withdrawals, and that Purple 'wins in every case' with a $3,750 balance. The customer accepted Purple at [user_msg_3]. The agent verified him with DOB and email ([tool_call_19], logged at [tool_call_21]), checked accounts (none) at [tool_call_24], and opened a Purple Account at [tool_call_26].

errors.finding: The agent recommended Purple Account as the best fit for lowest ATM fees abroad and did not mention Purple's $2.50 per-withdrawal out-of-network fee. For out-of-network foreign withdrawals, Green Fee-Free is $0 + $0. Purple is $2.50 x 18 = $45.

The agent stated that 'both accounts charge $0 in Rho fees for foreign ATM withdrawals' for the customer's out-of-network pattern. It built its cost table on that ($0 Rho fees for Purple) and concluded Purple is 'strictly better' with a $3,750 balance. Per doc_checking_accounts_purple_account_012, which the agent had read at [tool_result_13], Purple charges $2.50 per out-of-network withdrawal, separate from operator surcharges. Its $30/month rebate is for ATM operator fees (doc_checking_accounts_purple_account_004). So Purple costs $45 in Rho fees and Green Fee-Free $0. The customer acted on this and chose Purple.
The agent opened account_class 'Purple Account'. The correct class is 'Green Fee-Free Account' (account_type checking, user mv93f8a7b2).

first_critical_error.description: The agent recommended Purple Account instead of Green Fee-Free and omitted, then explicitly denied, Purple's $2.50 out-of-network ATM fee. The customer opened Purple based on that recommendation.

root_cause: The agent anchored on Purple's travel features ($0 foreign ATM fee, operator-fee rebates). It ignored Purple's $2.50 out-of-network fee even after reading it, so its cost comparison was built on a false $0.
key_facts_for_grader: Correct account: Green Fee-Free Account, with $0 out-of-network and $0 foreign ATM fees (doc_checking_accounts_green_fee-free_account_005)
Purple charges $2.50 per out-of-network withdrawal (doc_checking_accounts_purple_account_012), which is $45 over 18 withdrawals; its $0 foreign fee does not remove this
The agent read purple_account_012 at tool_result_13, then said at assistant_msg_3 that Purple charges $0 Rho fees for his withdrawals
The agent opened account_class 'Purple Account' at tool_call_26
Verification (DOB + email) was done and logged at tool_call_21 before the account lookup and opening; no verification issue
acceptable_variations: First critical error may be placed at assistant_msg_2 (recommendation) or assistant_msg_3 (misinformation used to confirm it); both precede tool_call_26

A judge may discuss Purple's $30/month operator-surcharge rebate as a possible offset. With correct figures, Purple beats Green Fee-Free only if average operator surcharges exceed $2.50, which the KB does not establish. The agent's comparison was based on a false $0 Rho fee for Purple, so the recommendation still fails.
adjudicator_notes: Agrees with the benchmark gold (Green Fee-Free Account), DB reward 0, and the prior gold for kimi-k3__task_075__t0, which failed a Purple recommendation that dismissed the $2.50 out-of-network fee.

summary: The customer wanted a referral link for a mailed Crypto-Cash Back card referral offer ($100 per referral who spends $500 in the first 2 months). The agent correctly declined to provide the get_referral_link tool at [assistant_msg_2], because no Crypto-Cash Back referral program is documented. At [user_msg_2] the customer asked for a transfer to a human who could verify the mailed offer, and at [assistant_msg_3] the agent refused, saying it can't transfer for an unverified referral offer. It then sent her to guessed app menu labels and external phone/chat channels ([assistant_msg_4]). The case calls for transfer_to_human_agents with reason unconfirmed_external_communication, which never happened.

customer_requests.request: Get a referral link for the mailed Crypto-Cash Back card referral offer ($100 per referral spending $500 in first 2 months)
customer_requests.correct_handling: Search the KB. No Crypto-Cash Back referral program is documented (crypto-cash_back_001–009 contain none; documented programs such as EcoCard $50/$500 in 60 days and Silver Rewards $75/$750 in 60 days do not match). Do not give get_referral_link; explain why (doc 009). No identity verification needed.
customer_requests.agent_handling: Searched the KB, found no documented Crypto-Cash Back referral program, and declined to give the referral-link tool, explaining that the card and terms are not documented.

customer_requests.request: Transfer to a human agent who can look up/verify the targeted mailer offer (explicitly asked at user_msg_2)
customer_requests.correct_handling: The customer claims a specific offer exists from an official-looking letter that cannot be verified in the KB. Doc 042 Tier 2 code unconfirmed_external_communication covers exactly this case. Offer or accept the transfer and call transfer_to_human_agents with reason 'unconfirmed_external_communication'.
customer_requests.agent_handling: Refused the transfer at [assistant_msg_3]: 'I also can't transfer this specific request to a human agent solely to pursue an unavailable/unverified referral offer'. It sent the customer to check the app and to call 1-800-RHO-BANK, use in-app chat, or visit rhobank.com/help ([assistant_msg_4]). transfer_to_human_agents was never called.

errors.finding: The customer cited an unverifiable mailed Rho-Bank offer and explicitly asked for a human who could verify targeted offers. The agent refused the transfer. Doc 042 Tier 2 lists unconfirmed_external_communication for a customer who claims a promotion exists from a letter, email or flyer that cannot be found in the KB, so the agent should have called transfer_to_human_agents with that reason. No transfer was made in the conversation.

Gave guessed app navigation ('credit card account dashboard' > sections labeled Referrals / Referral Center / Rewards / Promotional Offers) that is not documented for credit-card referrals. It also redirected the customer to external support channels (1-800-RHO-BANK, in-app chat, rhobank.com/help) to verify the offer, though she is already talking to support and a transfer was available.

Exposed internal handling rules to the customer ('agents can't generate the link on a customer's behalf', 'links must be generated ... only when the card has a documented referral program', 'can't transfer this specific request'), which is borderline under guideline 7.

first_critical_error.description: Refused the customer's explicit transfer request for an unverifiable mailed offer. It should have transferred via transfer_to_human_agents with reason unconfirmed_external_communication.

root_cause: The agent applied doc 009's 'Do not transfer to a human in these cases' clause and missed the more specific doc 042 code for unverifiable external communications such as mailed letters. It then deflected the customer to external channels instead.
key_facts_for_grader: No referral program is documented for the Crypto-Cash Back card; declining to give get_referral_link was correct
The claimed $100 / $500-in-2-months terms match no documented program
The customer explicitly asked for a human transfer at user_msg_2; the agent refused at assistant_msg_3
Expected action: transfer_to_human_agents with reason unconfirmed_external_communication (doc 042 Tier 2)
transfer_to_human_agents was never called
No identity verification was needed
acceptable_variations: A judge relying on doc 009's 'Do not transfer to a human in these cases' could argue that refusing the transfer is defensible. This gold rules the doc 042 external-communication code controlling because the customer cited a mailed letter and explicitly requested a transfer
A judge may categorize the critical error as policy_misapplication or incomplete instead of transfer_error
adjudicator_notes: Policy conflict, as noted in prior task_014 gold: doc 009 says not to give the link tool and 'Do not transfer to a human' when no referral program is documented, while doc 042's unconfirmed_external_communication code fits a customer holding a letter for an offer that cannot be verified. The prior gold (gpt-5.6-sol t2 pass with transfer; qwen3.8-max t1 fail for an accepted but unexecuted transfer) adjudicated the transfer as correct, matching the required docs (042 included, 009 not) and the benchmark gold. Those notes called declining without a transfer 'a defensible alternative'. Here I hold that once the customer explicitly asks for a human to verify the mailed offer, refusing the transfer fails, because 042 has a code for exactly this scenario. Confidence is medium because of this doc conflict. The customer did not abandon: she accepted the deflection and ended the chat, so there is no reason to exclude.

summary: Yuki Nakamura wanted to close her Business Silver Rewards Card (cc_224959b99e_bsilver) because she found a better card elsewhere. The agent verified her and paid the $125.00 balance from checking account 05 ([tool_call_18]). It checked disputes, pending replacements and closure history (all empty) and logged 'found_better_card' ([tool_call_32]). It then skipped Step 4 of the retention protocol: it never asked what attracted her to the competitor and never recommended the Business Platinum Rewards Card. Instead it went straight to the mid-tier $20/2,000-point retention offer at [assistant_msg_5], and the customer was offended and left ([user_msg_5]).

customer_requests.request: Pay off the $125.00 Business Silver balance from her Rho-Bank checking account so the card can be closed
customer_requests.correct_handling: Look up the checking account (05, Green, $2,850.00) and call pay_credit_card_from_checking_9182(user_id='224959b99e', checking_account_id='05', credit_card_account_id='cc_224959b99e_bsilver', amount=125.0).
customer_requests.agent_handling: The customer authorized the payment at [user_msg_3]. The agent looked up account 05 at [tool_call_14] and paid exactly $125.00 at [tool_call_18], bringing the balance to $0.00.

customer_requests.request: Close the Business Silver Rewards Card because she found a better card (handled through the retention protocol)
customer_requests.correct_handling: Step 1: confirm eligibility (no disputes, no pending replacement, account open 60+ days, $0 balance). Step 2: get_closure_reason_history_8293 (none). Step 3: log 'found_better_card'. Step 4: ask what features attracted her to the competitor (3x travel/advertising, no foreign transaction fees) and recommend the Rho-Bank Business Platinum Rewards Card (4% on travel, software and media/advertising, 0% foreign transaction fee). Step 5: only if she still wants to close, make the mid-tier retention offer (2,000 points or $20 statement credit). She would accept the $20 credit, so apply_statement_credit_8472(amount=20.0, reason='retention_offer') and keep the card open.
customer_requests.agent_handling: Steps 1-3 were done correctly ([tool_call_28], [tool_call_29], [tool_call_30], [tool_call_32]). The agent skipped Step 4: it never asked about the competitor's features or offered an alternative Rho-Bank card. It made the $20/2,000-point retention offer immediately at [assistant_msg_5], and the customer ended the chat in frustration at [user_msg_5]. No statement credit was applied.

customer_requests.request: Redeem the 4,500 points as a $45 statement credit
customer_requests.correct_handling: No agent tool exists for rewards redemption. Explain the options ($45 at 1 cent/point as a statement credit or checking deposit) and that the customer redeems them herself. Note that rewards remain redeemable for 45 days after a closure request.
customer_requests.agent_handling: At [assistant_msg_4], said it had no tool to redeem points and explained in-app redemption of 4,500 points for $45. At [assistant_msg_3] and [assistant_msg_5], it correctly mentioned the 45-day redemption window.

errors.finding: Skipped Step 4 of the retention protocol ('Found a better card: ask what features attracted them; if Rho-Bank offers a card with similar or better benefits, offer to help them apply'). The agent went straight to the Step 5 mid-tier retention offer (2,000 points or $20 credit). It should have asked about the competitor's features (3x travel and advertising, no foreign transaction fees) and recommended the Business Platinum Rewards Card (4% travel/software/media-advertising, 0% FX fee) before making any retention offer. The customer was offended and left, so the retention credit (apply_statement_credit_8472, $20.0, 'retention_offer') was never applied.
The agent first told the customer to 'please pay the remaining balance' without mentioning that it could pay from her checking account. The customer asked for it, and the agent then did so correctly.

first_critical_error.description: After logging 'found_better_card', the agent went straight to the $20 / 2,000-point retention offer. It never asked about the competitor's features or recommended the Business Platinum Rewards Card (Step 4), so the customer left and the retention credit was never applied.

root_cause: The agent jumped from logging the closure reason to the Step 5 retention offer and skipped the reason-specific Step 4 handling for 'found_better_card', which requires asking about the competitor's features and offering a comparable Rho-Bank card.
key_facts_for_grader: The $125.00 payment from checking 05 to cc_224959b99e_bsilver (tool_call_18) was correct and customer-authorized
Disputes, pending replacements and closure-reason history were all empty; 'found_better_card' was correctly logged (tool_call_32)
The agent never asked about the competitor card's features and never recommended the Business Platinum Rewards Card (4% travel/software/media-advertising, 0% foreign transaction fee)
The mid-tier retention offer ($20 or 2,000 points) was made at assistant_msg_5 without the Step 4 alternative-card recommendation; the customer then left
apply_statement_credit_8472 ($20.0, retention_offer) was never called; the card was neither retained nor closed
acceptable_variations: A judge may describe the error as policy_misapplication or incomplete instead of order_violation; any label is fine if it identifies the skipped Step 4 / missing Business Platinum recommendation
A judge may or may not flag the agent's initial 'please pay the balance' wording at assistant_msg_3 as minor
Paying the balance before the retention steps is consistent with Step 1 of the protocol
adjudicator_notes: Consistent with the earlier task_045 golds: kimi-k3__task_045__t2 passed with the Business Platinum recommendation followed by the $20 credit, and gpt-5.6-sol__task_045__t2 failed. The customer leaving was a scripted reaction to the agent skipping the alternative-card step, not a simulator fault, so the trace is included. The customer's request to redeem points was a reasonable off-script addition and did not affect the outcome.

summary: The customer wanted to close an empty Green checking account (61d4e5f6a7b8c901, opened 10/01/2025) and open a savings account; their only other checking account is a Silver Account opened 11/04/2025 (10 days old). The agent correctly identified the $25 mid-tier early-closure fee and granted deposit_check_3847 for the customer's $25 check [tool_call_20], but when the customer asked to close first, it closed the Green Account [tool_call_23] without explaining that this would leave no checking account meeting the 14-day tenure rule for opening savings. No savings account was ever opened and the agent wrapped up [assistant_msg_5].

customer_requests.request: Open a personal savings account
customer_requests.correct_handling: Savings eligibility requires a checking account held at least 14 days; only the Green checking (opened 10/01/2025) qualifies, the Silver checking (opened 11/04/2025) is only 10 days old. The savings account must therefore be opened BEFORE closing Green; when the customer asked to close first, the agent should have explained this dependency. Then discover needs and recommend the single best fit (Silver Plus Account per prior adjudication: 12-15 withdrawals/month, $2,500-$4,000 balance, daily compounding, ATM rebates, relationship bonus, savings goals) and call open_bank_account_4821(user_id='mm61b4c8d3', account_type='savings', account_class='Silver Plus Account'), then handle funding.
customer_requests.agent_handling: Stated the customer was eligible for savings [assistant_msg_3] (true only while Green existed) and listed options, but when the customer asked to do the closure first it simply agreed, closed Green [tool_call_23], and never opened a savings account or warned that the customer had just become ineligible until the Silver account reaches 14 days (11/18/2025).

customer_requests.request: Deposit a $25 check into the Green checking account to cover the early-closure fee
customer_requests.correct_handling: Give deposit_check_3847 and instruct the customer to call deposit_check_3847(account_id='61d4e5f6a7b8c901', check_amount=25).
customer_requests.agent_handling: Granted deposit_check_3847 with account_id 61d4e5f6a7b8c901 and check_amount 25 [tool_call_20] and explained it [assistant_msg_4].

customer_requests.request: Close the Green checking account (61d4e5f6a7b8c901)
customer_requests.correct_handling: Green Account (checking) is mid tier: $25 early-closure fee within 60 days (opened 10/01/2025, 44 days ago), 3-day notice period; balance must be at least $25 since the fee is deducted from the balance; status OPEN, no pending transactions. Close with close_bank_account_7392(account_id='61d4e5f6a7b8c901') without waiving the fee — but only after the savings account has been opened.
customer_requests.agent_handling: Correctly explained the $25 fee [assistant_msg_3], re-checked balance ($25.00) and transactions [tool_call_21, tool_call_22], and closed with waive_early_closure_fee=false [tool_call_23]. The closure mechanics were correct, but it was done before opening savings, destroying the customer's savings eligibility.

errors.finding: Closed the Green checking account (opened 10/01/2025) before opening the requested savings account, without explaining the consequence. After closure the only remaining checking account is Silver (opened 11/04/2025, 10 days old), which fails the 14-day checking-tenure requirement for opening savings, so the customer can no longer open savings. Policy-consistent handling was to explain the dependency and open savings first, then close Green.

Wrapped up after the closure without opening the savings account or telling the customer they are now ineligible until the Silver account reaches 14 days of tenure (11/18/2025). open_bank_account_4821 was unlocked but never called.

first_critical_error.description: Closed Green checking 61d4e5f6a7b8c901 before opening the savings account, leaving only the 10-day-old Silver checking and making the customer ineligible for savings under the 14-day tenure rule.

root_cause: The agent did not reason about how closing the only 14+-day-old checking account would affect the savings-eligibility check, and simply followed the customer's requested order instead of explaining why savings must be opened first.
key_facts_for_grader: Green checking 61d4e5f6a7b8c901 opened 10/01/2025; Silver checking 61e5f6a7b8c9d012 opened 11/04/2025 (10 days before 11/14/2025)
Savings opening requires a checking account held at least 14 days, so savings had to be opened before closing Green
Agent closed Green at tool_call_23 without opening savings; open_bank_account_4821 was never called
The $25 mid-tier early-closure fee was correctly identified, covered by the customer's $25 check (deposit_check_3847 granted at tool_call_20), and not waived
acceptable_variations: A judge may cite assistant_msg_4 (agreeing to proceed with closure first without explaining the dependency) as the first critical error instead of tool_call_23
A judge may categorize the error as incomplete (savings never opened) rather than order_violation; both describe the same failure
Not flagging the closure-before-notice-period (3 days) or the lack of needs discovery is acceptable
adjudicator_notes: The customer said 'the savings account can wait' [user_msg_3] and later 'That's everything I needed' [user_msg_5], but both are scripted reactions: the script says the customer accepts savings-first once given a reason, and the agent never gave one. Not simulator corruption. Consistent with the prior task_061 gold, which credited explaining the 14-day ordering dependency as required behavior. That counts as customer-stated information the agent correctly relied on. I considered excluding (the simulator fabricated a fact that drove the DB mismatch), but the agent's behavior is fully judgeable from its view, so I pass with a DB override. On provisional credit this run did what prior gold kimi-k3__task_039__t3 says is correct (three largest eligible charges, $129.45 false).
